This policy meets 10A NCAC 13G .0906 item 10 (Visitation in Facility & Sign Out Log) (and 10A NCAC 13F .0906): the visitor policy is in Procedures 1-9, and the resident sign-out/sign-in log is in Procedures 10-16. During a declared disaster or emergency, the facility follows G.S. 131D-7.1 and 131D-7.2, which protect residents' visitation rights, and the visitation protocols set by the Secretary of NC DHHS (Procedures 17-19).

definitions.definition: Any person who comes to see a resident, including family, friends, clergy, volunteers and other guests.
A visit that supports a resident's physical, emotional or spiritual well-being, such as end-of-life visits or visits to a resident who is distressed or declining.
A written record of each time a resident leaves or returns to the facility, other than for a medical emergency.
A state of disaster or emergency declared under North Carolina law, during which the NC DHHS Secretary may set visitation protocols.

procedures: Visiting hours are [VISITING HOURS]. Visitors may come outside these hours with the Administrator's or person in charge's approval, and always for compassionate care visits. Hours are posted at the entrance and given to each resident and responsible person at admission.
Visitors enter through [MAIN ENTRANCE] and sign the Visitor Log with date, name, resident visited, time in and time out. Staff greet visitors and direct them to the resident.
Residents choose who may visit. A resident may refuse any visitor. Staff ask the resident whether to allow a visitor if the resident is able to decide, and respect the answer.

Residents may visit privately in their rooms, if roommates agree and nothing stops it for health or safety reasons, or in [PRIVATE VISITING AREA]. Staff do not listen to or read private conversations or mail.
Residents may use a phone privately, and may send and receive mail unopened (G.S. 131D-21). A phone is available at [LOCATION] and staff help residents place calls on request.

Visitors must follow infection control rules posted at the entrance, such as hand hygiene or masks during an outbreak (see INF-04). Visitors may not bring alcohol or drugs, or smoke or vape outside designated areas (see SMK-01 and ALC-01).

The Administrator or person in charge may restrict or stop a visit only when a visitor threatens the safety or health of a resident, other residents or staff, such as when the visitor is violent, intoxicated, disruptive or ill with a contagious condition. The reason, the people involved and the action taken are recorded on an incident note (INC-01).
A visitor suspected of abusing, neglecting or exploiting a resident is handled under INC-03. Staff protect the resident's safety first.
Residents and families may raise visitation concerns through the Administrator or GRV-01. The facility does not retaliate.

Sign-out: Each resident who leaves the facility, other than for a medical emergency, is signed out on the Resident Sign-Out/Sign-In Log. The resident, a family member or staff enters: resident name, date, time out, destination, name and phone number of the person accompanying the resident, and the expected return time.
Staff check the log at the start of each shift and at each meal. They identify residents who are out and note expected return times.
Sign-in: On return, staff record the time in and the staff member's initials. Staff observe the resident's condition and report any injury or change to the person in charge (see HLT-03).
If a resident has not returned by the expected time plus [NUMBER] minutes, staff call the contact on the log. If the resident cannot be reached or located, the facility follows MIS-01.
Residents who are cognitively impaired or at risk of wandering are signed out only with a responsible adult, in line with the resident's care plan and WAN-01.

Medication needs during an absence are handled under MED-01 and MED-02. Staff prepare medications for the outing as the physician's orders and facility policy allow, and record what was given to the accompanying person.
The log is kept in [LOCATION], not in a place where other visitors can read resident information, and is retained under REC-01.
The Administrator reviews the logs weekly for completeness and patterns, such as frequent late returns, and follows up with staff or residents as needed.

During a declared disaster or emergency, the Administrator follows the visitation protocols set by the NC DHHS Secretary under G.S. 131D-7.1 and recognizes the visitation rights of residents under G.S. 131D-7.2. The Administrator checks current NC DHHS guidance at the start of the declaration and whenever it changes.

The facility may add safety precautions, such as screening, masking, scheduled times or designated areas, when guidance allows. It does not deny visitation in ways that the law or current protocols do not allow. Compassionate care and end-of-life visits are always allowed with precautions.

The Administrator tells residents, families and staff in writing and by posting any temporary change to visitation, explains the reason and expected length, and records the dates. Normal visitation resumes as soon as the declaration or guidance allows.

responsibilities.duty: Sets and posts visiting hours, approves any restriction, follows disaster-period visitation protocols and reviews logs weekly.
Welcomes visitors, enforces safety rules fairly, checks the sign-out log each shift and starts MIS-01 if a resident is overdue.
Help residents with visits and calls, complete sign-out/sign-in entries and report concerns.
Sign in and out, follow posted rules and respect residents' privacy and rights.

documentation: Posted visiting hours and visitor policy
Visitor Log
Resident Sign-Out/Sign-In Log
Incident notes for any restricted visit
Written notices of temporary visitation changes during emergencies
Weekly log review notes

policies.title: Smoking Policy
policies.applies_to: ACH and FCH
policies.purpose: To protect residents, staff and visitors from fire and smoke exposure. This policy sets where smoking is allowed, how residents who smoke are assessed and supervised, and what happens when the smoking rules are not followed.
policies.policy:
[AGENCY NAME] prohibits smoking inside the building. Smoking by residents, staff and visitors is allowed only in the designated outdoor smoking area(s) at [ADDRESS]. This policy meets 10A NCAC 13F .1211(11), 10A NCAC 13F .0704(2) and 10A NCAC 13G .0704(2).

Item 11a — Smoking: Designated areas outside of the building / No smoking inside the facility. Smoking is never permitted inside the home. This includes resident rooms, bathrooms, hallways, common areas, the kitchen, vehicles used for resident transport and any area where oxygen is stored or used. The designated outdoor area is located away from doors, windows, air intakes and oxygen storage. It is equipped with a covered, non-combustible ash receptacle and a fire extinguisher, and it is visible from a staff observation point. The area is marked with a "Designated Smoking Area" sign, and "No Smoking" signs are posted at entrances and inside the building.

Item 11b — Smoking: Plan for on-going assessment and increased supervision of residents who smoke, if needed. Every resident is asked about tobacco and vaping use at pre-admission screening and again at admission. Each resident who smokes is assessed for fire-safety risk: cognition and judgment, vision, hand dexterity and tremor, mobility, sedating medications, oxygen use and history of burns or unsafe smoking. The assessment is repeated at each reassessment, after any change of condition, and after any unsafe-smoking incident. Residents found to be at risk are placed on increased supervision, which is written into the care plan. Supervision may include staff presence during each smoking break, staff-held lighters and matches, a smoking apron, or a limited schedule of supervised smoking times. A resident who is assessed as unable to smoke safely, even with supervision, may smoke only while directly supervised. Residents who use oxygen may not smoke within the oxygen-use areas and must follow the oxygen safety rules in their care plan.

Item 11c — Smoking: What are the consequences of non-compliance with smoking policies? Residents are told of the following consequences at admission, in the resident contract (CON-01) and at orientation. A resident who smokes in a prohibited area, leaves lit smoking materials unattended, or ignores supervision requirements receives: (1) an immediate verbal correction and removal of the hazard; (2) a written notice and care plan review after a second occurrence; (3) restriction to supervised smoking, with smoking materials held by staff, after a third occurrence or any occurrence that creates an immediate fire risk; and (4) if the behavior continues and endangers the health or safety of residents or staff, a discharge review under ADM-05, which follows the State's notice and hearing-appeal requirements. Staff who allow or take part in indoor smoking or who fail to supervise as required are subject to discipline up to termination. Visitors who do not follow the policy are asked to leave the property. Failure to enforce the rules may also result in a State citation, so every incident is documented.

definitions.definition: The outdoor location approved by the Administrator where smoking is allowed, away from the building and from oxygen.
Added staff oversight, written into the care plan, for a resident whose assessment shows unsafe smoking risk.
Cigarettes, cigars, pipes, e-cigarettes and vaping devices, lighters and matches.

procedures: Before admission, the Administrator or designee asks every applicant about tobacco and vaping use and records the answer on the pre-admission screening (ADM-01).

At admission, staff give the resident and responsible person a copy of this policy, explain the designated areas and the consequences of non-compliance, and obtain a signed acknowledgment, which is filed in the resident record.
Within the time frame set for the initial assessment (ADM-02), a trained staff member completes the smoking risk assessment for each resident who smokes. The Administrator or Manager reviews it.
The care plan (ADM-03) records whether the resident may smoke independently or needs increased supervision, who supervises, how smoking materials are stored, and any oxygen restrictions.
The Administrator designates the outdoor smoking area(s) in writing, posts all signs, and ensures a fire extinguisher and a non-combustible, covered ash receptacle are in place.
The Manager or supervisor-in-charge checks the smoking area at least once each shift and empties ash receptacles into a metal container, kept outside the building, at least daily.
Staff collect and store lighters and matches for residents on increased supervision in a locked location and issue them only for supervised smoking.
Staff remind any resident, visitor or staff member smoking in a prohibited area to stop and move to the designated area, and they remove any lit material immediately.
Staff record each non-compliance event in an incident note, apply the consequence steps in the order listed in the policy, and notify the Administrator the same day.
If an incident involves fire, burns or injury, staff follow INC-01 and FIR-01. They notify the physician and responsible person as required and complete the incident report.
The Administrator reviews every smoking incident and, if the resident's needs have changed, requests a reassessment and care plan revision within the agency's required time frame.
Smoking risk assessments are repeated at every scheduled reassessment, after any change of condition, and after any incident. The care plan is updated when supervision needs change.
Staff smoke only on break and only in the designated area, and they do not smoke or vape in view of residents on supervised status.
The Administrator reviews smoking incidents quarterly as part of quality assurance (GOV-04) and corrects any pattern, such as a poorly placed smoking area or inadequate supervision.
The Administrator reviews this policy annually and when the rules change (GOV-03).

responsibilities.duty: Designates and maintains the smoking area, enforces consequences, reviews incidents and the policy, and decides on discharge review.
Checks the smoking area each shift, ensures supervision happens as care planned, and reports incidents to the Administrator.
Supervise residents who smoke as care planned, secure smoking materials, correct violations and document them.
Follow the policy, smoke only in the designated area and accept supervision when assessed as needed.

documentation: Signed smoking policy acknowledgment
Smoking risk assessments and reassessments
Care plan entries on smoking supervision
Smoking incident notes and incident reports
Smoking area inspection log
Annual policy review record

policies.title: Alcohol Use and Substance Abuse Policy
policies.applies_to: ACH and FCH
policies.purpose: To make sure resident alcohol use is assessed and communicated to the physician, alcohol is stored and monitored only under a physician's order, and substance misuse is prevented. This policy also states the consequences of non-compliance.
policies.policy:
[AGENCY NAME] respects residents' choices and also protects their safety. Residents may not keep, use or be given alcohol in the home unless a physician has ordered it. Illegal drugs, misuse of prescription medication and diversion of medication are prohibited. This policy meets 10A NCAC 13G .0704(2) as listed on the application checklist.

Item 12a — Alcohol Use: Assessment of resident and communication with doctor regarding alcohol consumption. At pre-admission screening, at admission, at every reassessment and after any change of condition, staff ask the resident and responsible person about current and past alcohol use. The assessment covers type, amount, frequency, recent changes, history of withdrawal, falls, confusion or intoxication, and the medications the resident takes. The Administrator or designee communicates the findings to the resident's physician, asks for a written order or direction about whether alcohol is permitted and under what limits, and records the physician's response. Staff report any observed intoxication, withdrawal symptoms or new or increased use to the physician and responsible person promptly (HLT-03).

Item 12b — Alcohol Use: Safekeeping and monitoring of alcohol with physician's order. Alcohol is kept and offered only when the physician's order is on file. The order states the type, amount, frequency and any conditions. Alcohol is stored in locked storage, labeled with the resident's name, and is not kept in resident rooms. When alcohol is part of the order, it is handled like a medication order: it is entered on the MAR, given only by staff who meet 10A NCAC 13F Rule .0403, within one hour before or after the scheduled time, and charted immediately after it is given, with no pre-charting (see 10A NCAC 13F .1004, MED-01). Staff monitor the resident for effects and record the amount consumed. If a resident or visitor brings alcohol into the home without an order, staff take it into locked safekeeping, record it, and contact the physician for direction. Without an order, it is returned to the responsible person or removed from the premises.

Item 12c — Alcohol Use: What are the consequences of non-compliance with alcohol and substance abuse policies? Residents are told of the consequences at admission, in the resident contract (CON-01) and at orientation. If a resident drinks without an order, keeps alcohol in a room, uses illegal drugs or misuses medication, the home responds in steps: (1) staff remove the item, ensure safety, and tell the physician and responsible person; (2) the Administrator meets with the resident and responsible person, issues a written notice and updates the care plan; (3) if misuse continues, the home may impose supervised-only access or other care-plan limits; and (4) if the behavior endangers the health or safety of the resident or others, or the resident's needs cannot be met, the home may begin discharge review under ADM-05, following the State's notice and appeal requirements. Illegal drug use or sale, or diversion of another resident's medication, is reported to law enforcement as appropriate. Staff who use or possess alcohol or illegal drugs on duty, or who are impaired at work, are removed from duty immediately and are disciplined up to termination.

definitions.definition: A written order from the resident's licensed prescriber that states what alcohol may be used, how much, how often and under what conditions.
Holding a resident's alcohol in locked storage, labeled and logged, with access controlled by staff.
Use of illegal drugs, misuse of prescription or over-the-counter medicine, or use of alcohol outside a physician's order.

procedures: At pre-admission screening, the Administrator or designee asks about alcohol and substance use and records the answers (ADM-01).
At admission and each reassessment, the Manager or a trained staff member completes the alcohol use assessment, covering type, amount, frequency, history and medication interactions.

Within [NUMBER] business days of admission or any change in use, the Administrator or designee contacts the physician and shares the assessment findings. Staff record the date, who they spoke with and the physician's direction in the resident record.
The Administrator obtains a written physician order before any alcohol is stored or offered. If there is no order, alcohol is not permitted.
Staff store ordered alcohol in a locked cabinet, labeled with the resident's name and the order, and count or measure the quantity when received.
Ordered alcohol is entered on the MAR and given only by a staff member authorized under 10A NCAC 13F Rule .0403, within 1 hour before or after the scheduled time, and charted immediately (MED-01).
Staff record the amount consumed, the resident's response and any side effects. They notify the physician of concerns such as falls, drowsiness, confusion or interaction with medications.
Staff who find alcohol in a room or in a visitor's possession without an order secure it, log it, and notify the Manager the same shift.
The Administrator contacts the physician about found alcohol and either obtains an order or returns the alcohol to the responsible person or removes it from the premises. This is documented.
Staff who see signs of intoxication or withdrawal check the resident's safety and vital signs as trained, notify the physician or call 911 as needed, and follow HLT-03.

Suspected illegal drug use, medication misuse or diversion is reported to the Administrator immediately. The Administrator notifies the physician and responsible person, secures the evidence and decides whether to notify law enforcement.
The Administrator applies the consequence steps in the policy in order, issues written notices, documents each meeting and updates the care plan (ADM-03).
If discharge is considered, the Administrator follows ADM-05 and does not discharge without the required written notice and Hearing Request Form.
Staff attend training on this policy at orientation and annually (STF-03). The Administrator investigates any staff impairment, suspends the staff member from duty and documents it.
The Administrator reviews alcohol and substance incidents quarterly in the quality assurance process (GOV-04) and reviews this policy annually (GOV-03).

responsibilities.duty: Ensures assessment, physician communication and orders are in place; imposes consequences; investigates incidents and staff impairment.
Completes assessments, secures and logs alcohol, and ensures only authorized staff give ordered alcohol.
Administers ordered alcohol per the MAR, charts immediately and reports adverse effects.
Gives or declines orders for alcohol and gives direction on monitoring.
Disclose alcohol and substance use, follow the policy and do not bring alcohol or drugs into the home without an order.

documentation: Alcohol use assessment
Physician communication log and orders
MAR entries for ordered alcohol
Alcohol safekeeping and consumption log
Incident notes and written notices
Signed contract and orientation acknowledgment
Staff training record

policies.title: Activities Program and Calendar
policies.applies_to: ACH and FCH
policies.purpose: To provide residents with a planned, varied activities program that meets the required hours, reflects resident assessments and preferences, and is posted with beginning and end times for each activity.
policies.policy:
[AGENCY NAME] operates an activities program that offers scheduled activities in the home and in the community and adapts them to each resident's assessment, interests and abilities. This policy meets Item 13 — Activities Program: Sample calendar (meets hour requirements/times listed, variety of activities and outings; calendar must contain beginning and end times of activities), 10A NCAC 13F/13G .0905(c)(2)(d).

Every calendar lists each activity with a beginning and an end time. The Administrator checks the total scheduled hours against the minimum required by the rule before the calendar is posted and records the total on the calendar. The calendar includes physical, social, creative, cognitive, spiritual and community activities, plus regular outings. Residents who prefer to stay in their rooms, who are on bed rest, or who cannot join group activities are offered individual in-room activities at least as often as group activities are offered to others, and these are documented. Participation is voluntary. Residents are never required to attend an activity.

Sample weekly calendar (times are beginning–end):
Monday: 9:00–9:45 Morning stretch and chair exercise; 10:00–11:00 News and current events discussion; 2:00–3:00 Bingo; 6:30–7:30 Movie night.
Tuesday: 9:00–9:45 Chair exercise; 10:30–11:30 Arts and crafts; 2:00–3:30 Music and sing-along; 6:30–7:15 Card and board games.
Wednesday: 9:00–9:45 Chair exercise; 10:00–12:00 Community outing (park, scenic drive or local shopping); 2:00–3:00 Devotional or faith discussion; 6:30–7:30 Reminiscence and storytelling.
Thursday: 9:00–9:45 Chair exercise; 10:30–11:30 Gardening or plant care; 2:00–3:00 Birthday social and resident council; 6:30–7:30 Puzzles and trivia.
Friday: 9:00–9:45 Chair exercise; 10:30–11:30 Baking or cooking activity; 1:30–3:30 Outing (library, restaurant or community event); 6:30–7:30 Movie night.
Saturday: 10:00–11:00 Faith service (live or broadcast); 2:00–3:30 Family and friends social and games; 6:30–7:15 Music or video.
Sunday: 10:00–11:00 Faith service (live or broadcast); 2:00–3:00 Letter writing, phone or video calls; 6:30–7:30 Music or relaxing video.
This sample week schedules 27.25 hours of group activities, plus individual in-room activities, and it is replaced each month with the current month's calendar.

definitions.definition: The posted schedule of group and individual activities and outings, with a beginning and an end time for each.
A planned off-site activity with staff supervision and transportation as needed (see DLV-02).
A one-to-one or independent activity offered to a resident who does not take part in group events.

procedures: At admission, the Activity Coordinator or designee interviews the resident and responsible person about interests, past hobbies, faith practices, cultural preferences and abilities, and records them in the resident record.
The resident assessment and care plan (ADM-02, ADM-03) are used to identify activity needs, physical limits and cognitive level, including residents in the memory care unit (HLT-04).
By the 25th of each month, the Activity Coordinator drafts the next month's calendar with beginning and end times for every activity, and includes a variety of activities and outings.
The Activity Coordinator totals the scheduled hours and compares the total to the minimum hours required by the rule. The Administrator reviews, signs and dates the calendar.

The calendar is posted in a common area at residents' eye level, in large print, and copies are given to residents and responsible persons on request. Staff read it aloud for residents with vision limits.
The Activity Coordinator arranges supplies, space, staff support and transportation for each activity and for each outing, with staff ratios sufficient for resident safety.
Before any outing, staff confirm each participating resident's safety needs, medications and sign-out in the log (VIS-01), and take emergency contact information.
Staff encourage, but never force, participation. A resident who declines is offered an individual activity, and the refusal is noted.
Staff record attendance for each activity, noting each participant's name, date, activity and response, in an attendance log.
The Activity Coordinator offers in-room activities to residents who cannot attend group events and documents each contact.
If an activity is cancelled or changed, staff post a notice, tell residents, and record the reason. A substitute activity is offered with a new beginning and end time.
Each month the Activity Coordinator reviews attendance and resident feedback and adjusts the next calendar. Resident council input is documented (RR-01).
The Administrator reviews the calendar, hours and attendance quarterly in the quality assurance process (GOV-04) and keeps copies of past calendars for [NUMBER] months.
If a calendar is not completed or does not meet the required hours, the Administrator corrects it within 48 hours and records the correction.

responsibilities.duty: Approves the calendar, verifies the hours, provides resources and reviews attendance.
Interviews residents, prepares and posts the calendar, leads or arranges activities and keeps attendance logs.
Assist residents in attending activities and outings and report resident preferences.
Choose whether and how to take part and give feedback on activities.

documentation: Monthly activity calendars with beginning and end times and a total-hours note
Resident activity preference assessments
Attendance and in-room activity logs
Outing sign-out records
Resident council notes on activities

policies.title: Food Service, Menus and Therapeutic Diets
policies.applies_to: ACH and FCH
policies.purpose: To make sure residents receive nutritious, safely prepared meals according to written menus with portion sizes, and that therapeutic diets are provided only under physician orders from menus developed by a Registered Dietitian.
policies.policy:
[AGENCY NAME] provides meals and snacks from written, dated menus that show a portion size for each item. Therapeutic diets are provided only on a licensed prescriber's order. If the home accommodates therapeutic diets, each therapeutic diet menu is developed by a Registered Dietitian and bears the dietitian's signature and RD number. This policy meets Item 14 — Nutrition and Food Service: sample menu for one month with portion sizes; therapeutic diet menus developed by a Registered Dietitian with signature and RD number on each menu (10A NCAC 13F/13G .0509 and .0904(c)(d)).

Menus. A full one-month sample menu (Attachment A) lists each meal and snack with portion sizes expressed in measurable amounts. Sample day: Breakfast — 1 cup oatmeal, 1 medium banana, 1 slice whole-wheat toast with 1 teaspoon margarine, 8 oz 2% milk, coffee or tea. Lunch — 3 oz baked chicken, 1/2 cup mashed potatoes, 1/2 cup green beans, 1 dinner roll, 1/2 cup canned peaches, 8 oz water or juice. Supper — 1 cup vegetable-beef soup, 1 turkey sandwich (2 oz turkey on 2 slices of bread), 1/2 cup coleslaw, 1 small oatmeal cookie, 8 oz milk. Evening snack — 4 saltine crackers with 1 oz cheese, and 6 oz juice. Menus are planned to meet residents' nutritional needs and vary from day to day, with substitutions of similar nutritional value.

Therapeutic diets. The home accommodates therapeutic diets ordered by the physician and identified on the resident assessment. Examples are: no-added-sugar/consistent carbohydrate, low sodium, mechanically altered or pureed texture, and heart-healthy. For each diet accommodated, the home keeps a menu developed by the Registered Dietitian, [RD NAME], RD No. [RD NUMBER], who signs and dates each menu, shows the RD number on it, and reviews the menus at least annually or when the diet changes. If a diet ordered is not on file, the home does not begin it until a dietitian-approved menu is in place, or it decides whether the resident's needs can be met (ADM-04).

The home accommodates dietary needs from the physician's orders and the resident assessment, including allergies, texture limits, cultural and religious practices and preferences.

definitions.definition: The measurable serving amount for each food on the menu, such as 1/2 cup green beans or 3 oz chicken.
A diet ordered by a licensed prescriber to treat or manage a medical condition, such as a diabetic, low-sodium or texture-modified diet.
A credentialed dietitian who develops and signs therapeutic menus and records an RD number on each.

procedures: The Administrator and the cook plan menus at least [NUMBER] days before each month begins. Each menu names each food and its portion size, and the menu is dated.
Menus are posted where residents can see them. Staff read the menu to residents who cannot read it.

At admission and on each reassessment, the Manager records diet orders, allergies, texture needs, preferences and cultural or religious restrictions from the physician orders and the resident assessment.
For a diet order, the Manager gives the order to the cook, checks it matches the therapeutic diet menu, and enters it on the care plan (ADM-03).
The Administrator contracts with a Registered Dietitian to develop therapeutic diet menus. Each menu is signed and dated by the dietitian and shows the RD number.
The Administrator files the RD menus in the kitchen and in the administrative binder, and provides them at the licensure survey.
Cooks prepare and serve food according to the menu and recipes, using measuring tools to serve portions. Any substitution is written on the menu with the reason and is of similar nutritional value.
Residents with texture-modified or other special diets are served the correct diet, and staff verify the resident's name and diet card before each meal.
Staff provide meals at scheduled times and make snacks and fluids available, and they report to the Manager when a resident repeatedly refuses meals or loses weight.
The Manager notifies the physician and responsible person when a resident has a significant change in intake, weight, swallowing or appetite (HLT-03).
Kitchen staff follow sanitation requirements: handwashing, glove use, temperature control, cleaning, and safe storage (INF-01, INF-03, DLV-01).
The Administrator keeps menus as served, with substitutions noted, for [NUMBER] months and reviews them with residents' feedback at resident council.
The Administrator reviews menus, diets and the RD contract at least annually, and when residents' needs change, and records the review (GOV-04).

responsibilities.duty: Approves menus, contracts with the Registered Dietitian, and ensures diets match orders.
Prepare food by the menu and portion sizes, follow diet orders and sanitation rules.
Records diet orders, checks diet service, reports intake concerns to the physician.
Develops, signs and dates therapeutic diet menus with the RD number and reviews them at least annually.

documentation: One-month menu with portion sizes (Attachment A)
Therapeutic diet menus signed by the RD with RD number
Physician diet orders
Diet list and care plan diet entries
Menu substitution records
RD contract and review record

policies.title: Resident Contract and Admission Agreement
policies.applies_to: ACH and FCH
policies.purpose: To ensure every resident receives a written contract and a written statement of services and charges at admission, that the contract includes every area listed in the rule, and that it matches State discharge, notice and Special Assistance requirements.
policies.policy:
[AGENCY NAME] gives each resident and responsible person a written contract before or at admission, explains it and obtains signatures. This policy meets Item 15 — Resident Contract: a copy of the resident contract to be used upon admission, including all areas listed in the rule (10A NCAC 13F .0704 and 10A NCAC 13G .0704). The Administrator compares the contract against the current text of the rule at each annual policy review, so that every area the rule lists is present.

Under N.C.G.S. §131D-21, residents have the right to a written statement of services and charges on admission and to a copy of the residents' rights. The home gives both at admission and documents it.

The contract includes at least: the services and supplies provided and the basic rate; the charges for any extra services and when and how rates may change, with advance written notice; the payment terms and who is responsible for payment; the home's policies on smoking (SMK-01), alcohol and substance use (ALC-01), visitation (VIS-01), resident funds and property (RR-02), and grievances with ombudsman access (GRV-01); the refund and deposit terms (REF-01); and the conditions under which the home may discharge a resident. The facility-initiated discharge reasons stated in the contract match the rule: needs cannot be met, improved health, safety or health endangered, nonpayment after written warning, or legal mandate. Discharge notice is 30 days unless urgent, with the written Notice of Discharge and Hearing Request Form hand delivered the day it is dated and a copy to the responsible person, and the notice includes the ombudsman and discharge team contacts (10A NCAC 13F .0702). The contract states that the administrator may require up to 14 days' written notice from a resident who chooses to leave, except where delay would jeopardize health or safety (10A NCAC 13F .0702, resident-initiated discharge).

For State/County Special Assistance residents, the contract states that the home accepts the State rate as payment in full for room and board, and that the home will not charge above the maximum allowed.

definitions.definition: The signed written agreement between the home and the resident or responsible person describing services, charges, policies and rights.
The person who acts for the resident under legal authority or who is named by the resident to receive notices and make arrangements.
State/County program that helps eligible residents pay room and board; the home accepts the State-set rate as payment in full.

procedures: The Administrator prepares the standard contract with every area the rule lists and has it reviewed by [ATTORNEY OR CONSULTANT NAME] before first use.

Before admission, the Administrator or designee gives the applicant and responsible person a copy of the contract and the written statement of services and charges, and offers time to read it and ask questions.
At admission, the Administrator reviews each section in plain language, using an interpreter or other language access as needed (RR-05).
The Administrator gives the resident a copy of N.C.G.S. §131D-21 and the residents' rights statement and documents the delivery (RR-01).
The resident or legal representative, and the Administrator, sign and date the contract. A signed copy goes to the resident or responsible person and the original is filed in the resident record.
The contract lists the basic rate, what it includes, the extra charges and the date payment is due. The Administrator explains how the resident's funds are handled (RR-02).
The Administrator explains the 14-day notice requirement for a resident who wants to leave, and the exceptions for health or safety. The 14-day requirement is written into the contract.
The Administrator explains the 30-day discharge notice, the Hearing Request Form, the ombudsman and discharge team contacts, and the reasons for facility-initiated discharge (ADM-05).

For SA applicants, the Administrator confirms the rate, explains the home will accept the State rate and charges nothing above the maximum, and refers questions to the county Department of Social Services (GOV-05).
Any change to the contract is made in writing with advance notice to the resident and responsible person, signed by both and filed. Rate changes are not applied without notice.
If a resident leaves, the Administrator records the notice given, documents contacts with possible discharge locations, and handles refunds as the contract says (REF-01).
The Administrator checks every contract at admission for completeness and signatures and corrects missing items within [NUMBER] business days.
The Administrator reviews the contract against the current rule text and this policy at least annually and records the review (GOV-03).

responsibilities.duty: Maintains the contract, explains it, signs it, and ensures it matches the rules and discharge procedures.
Gives the contract and statement of services and charges before admission and files signed copies.
Read and sign the contract, meet payment terms and give required notice before leaving.
Applies contract charges accurately and applies the SA rate correctly.

documentation: Signed resident contract
Written statement of services and charges
Receipt for rights statement and N.C.G.S. §131D-21 copy
Contract amendment notices
Discharge notice records and discharge location contact log
Annual contract and rule comparison record

policies.title: Organization, Governing Body, Administrator and Manager Responsibilities
policies.applies_to: ACH and FCH
policies.purpose: To document the home's operational plan, including staffing patterns and the responsibility of each staff member, so the county adult home specialist and ACLS can see how the home is organized and who is in charge at all times.
policies.policy:
[AGENCY NAME] is owned and governed by [GOVERNING BODY / OWNER NAME], which appoints a certified administrator, is responsible for the home's compliance with G.S. Chapter 131D and 10A NCAC 13F or 13G, and provides the resources needed to operate safely.

This policy meets FCH-2.b(i) — County adult home specialist assesses the applicant's operational plan, with specific emphasis on staffing patterns and the responsibility of each staff member (License a Family Care Home, Procedures step 2.b). The operational plan is set out below and is kept current.

Administrator. The Administrator, [ADMINISTRATOR NAME], is responsible for the day-to-day operation of the home. For an adult care home (ACH), the Administrator is certified under N.C.G.S. §90-288.14 (age 21 or older, 120-hour Administrator-in-Training program, exam and criminal background check). For a family care home (FCH), approval under 10A NCAC 13G .1501 requires a high school diploma or GED, the State-approved 120-hour AIT program, the Administrator Exam, age 21 or older and a criminal background check; there is no renewal fee. See STF-05.

Manager and supervisor-in-charge. In the Administrator's absence, an ACH uses a designated manager (10A NCAC 13F .0102, per Rule .0402) and an FCH uses a supervisor-in-charge (10A NCAC 13G .0102, per Rule .0402). A manager is 21 or older, has a high school diploma or GED and completes 12 continuing education hours a year (this replaced the term "Administrator in Charge" effective 9/1/2024). The manager or supervisor-in-charge is named in writing for each period of administrator absence.

Staffing patterns. Shifts are the 1st 7:01 a.m.–3:00 p.m., the 2nd 3:01 p.m.–11:00 p.m. and the 3rd 11:01 p.m.–7:00 a.m. A home with 7–20 residents has at least one designated staff person per shift for personal care and supervision. A home with 7–12 residents has the administrator or manager on site or within 500 feet with two-way communication, and an awake staff member on duty if any resident is disoriented or wanders. A home with 81 or more residents has the administrator on duty 8 hours a day, 5 days a week. Further detail is in STF-01.

Operational plan and responsibilities by role. Administrator: overall operation, licensure, finances, hiring, training, quality assurance and resident rights. Manager / supervisor-in-charge: shift oversight, staff direction, resident care coordination and reporting to the Administrator. Personal care aides: personal care, supervision, activities of daily living, and reporting changes. Medication aides: medication administration under Rule .0403 and MAR documentation (MED-01). Cook / dietary staff: menus and meals (NUT-01). Housekeeping and maintenance: cleanliness, laundry and repairs (DLV-01). Activity coordinator: activities (ACT-01). Planned staffing per shift for this home: 1st shift [NUMBER] personal care aide(s) and [NUMBER] medication aide(s); 2nd shift [NUMBER] and [NUMBER]; 3rd shift [NUMBER] awake or on-site staff. [NUMBER] residents is the planned capacity.

definitions.definition: The certified (ACH) or approved (FCH) individual responsible for the operation of the home.
The person designated to run the home day to day in the administrator's absence, as defined in 10A NCAC 13F .0102 and Rule .0402.
The person in charge of the family care home in the administrator's absence, as defined in 10A NCAC 13G .0102 and Rule .0402.
The written description of how the home operates, including staffing patterns and each staff member's responsibilities.

procedures: The governing body appoints the Administrator in writing and confirms that the Administrator holds the required certification or approval. A copy is kept in the personnel file and administrative binder.

The Administrator verifies before hire or designation that each manager or supervisor-in-charge is 21 or older, has a high school diploma or GED, and will complete 12 CE hours a year, and records it in the personnel file (STF-02, STF-05).
The Administrator writes the operational plan, including the shift staffing pattern and the responsibilities of every position, and updates it whenever capacity, residents' needs or staffing change.

The Administrator sets the staffing pattern by shift to meet the minimums for the home's size: at least one designated staff person per shift for 7–20 residents; the administrator or manager on site or within 500 feet with two-way communication for 7–12 residents; an awake staff member if any resident is disoriented or wanders; and administrator on duty 8 hours a day, 5 days a week for 81 or more residents.
The Administrator posts a weekly schedule showing each person, position and shift, and records actual hours worked.
The Administrator names a manager or supervisor-in-charge in writing for every absence. All staff know who is in charge and how to reach that person ([PHONE]).
If the 500-foot option is used, the Administrator verifies that two-way communication works (phone or radio), tests it monthly and documents each test.
Each employee receives a written job description and sign-off on duties at hire and when duties change (STF-03).
The Administrator holds a staff meeting at least [NUMBER] times a year to review the operational plan and any changes.

For FCH licensure, the Administrator gives the operational plan to the county adult home specialist, who assesses it, with emphasis on staffing patterns and the responsibility of each staff member, and the Administrator answers questions and corrects gaps.
The governing body reviews compliance reports, incident trends and quality assurance findings at least quarterly (GOV-04) and records its decisions in minutes.
The Administrator notifies ACLS of any change in administrator or licensee as required (GOV-02) and reviews the operational plan annually (GOV-03).

responsibilities.duty: Appoints the Administrator, funds operations, reviews compliance and approves policies.
Runs the home, maintains the operational plan and staffing patterns, designates a manager or supervisor-in-charge, and ensures compliance.
Directs the home in the Administrator's absence and reports issues promptly.
Perform duties in their job descriptions and follow the chain of command.

documentation: Governing body appointment and minutes
Administrator certification or approval
Manager / supervisor-in-charge designations and CE records
Operational plan with staffing pattern and role duties
Weekly schedules and time records
Two-way communication test log
Signed job descriptions

policies.title: Licensure, Posting, Capacity, Renewal, Change of Licensee and Closure
policies.applies_to: ACH and FCH
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] is licensed by the NC DHHS Division of Health Service Regulation, Adult Care Licensure Section (ACLS), before it operates. It also sets out how the license is displayed and renewed, how capacity limits are kept, and how the home handles a change of licensee, a closing, or a licensure action.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] operates only under a current license issued by ACLS. Adult care homes (ACH, 7 or more beds) follow 10A NCAC 13F. Family care homes (FCH, 2-6 beds) follow 10A NCAC 13G. The license is posted in a publicly viewable place (10A NCAC 13F .0202; 10A NCAC 13G .0202). If a provisional license is issued, it and the DHSR notice of reasons are posted in place of the full license (N.C.G.S. §131D-2.7). The license is not transferable. The home is licensed only as the type of facility named on the license. The home never houses more residents than the capacity on the license (10A NCAC 13F .0206; 10A NCAC 13G .0206). Each ACH bed and service must comply with the Certificate of Need (CON). The home renews its license every year on a calendar-year basis. It gives at least 30 days' written notice before any change of licensee or closing. It tells residents in writing within 5 calendar days of receiving a notice of revocation.

definitions.definition: The NC DHHS Division of Health Service Regulation, Adult Care Licensure Section, which licenses and surveys adult care homes and family care homes.
The person or entity to whom the license is issued. The license cannot be transferred to anyone else.
A time-limited license issued by DHSR under N.C.G.S. §131D-2.7 when the home has not corrected violations or other grounds exist. It is posted with the DHSR notice of reasons.
The maximum number of residents shown on the license. For an FCH it is 2-6 residents, with ambulatory and non-ambulatory capacity listed separately. For an ACH it is 7 or more residents.
The person designated by the resident, or authorized by law, to receive notices and act for the resident.

procedures: Before applying, the [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] confirms the home type. A home with 7 or more beds is an ACH and a home with 2-6 beds is an FCH.

ACH only: the governing body obtains an approved Certificate of Need (CON) before filing the license application. No ACH license application is filed until the CON requirement is met (10A NCAC 13F .0204).

ACH application packet: the Administrator assembles the application, building plans, fire marshal report, sanitation report, license fee and certificate of occupancy. The Administrator confirms the initial fee with ACLS before payment. The DHSR page shows $400 plus $19 per bed, which conflicts with the fee schedule quoted on DHSR forms. The home pays the higher published figure unless ACLS confirms otherwise in writing.

FCH application packet: the Administrator submits the application through the county DSS adult home specialist. The packet includes the zoning approval letter, photographs, floor plans and the initial fee ($350). The county submits it to DHSR within 10 business days (10A NCAC 13G .0204).

The Administrator submits the operational policies and procedures to ACLS for approval (see GOV-03). Licensure depends on ACLS approval of the policies and on a pre-licensing survey. The Administrator schedules staff and records so they are ready for the survey.

The Administrator logs the date ACLS's written decision is received. ACLS gives written notice of its decision within 14 days. The Administrator also records the end of the initial 6-month license term and the date of the follow-up survey.

On the day a license is received, the Administrator posts it in the entrance area where residents and visitors can see it. A provisional license and the DHSR notice of reasons replace the full license on the wall until a full license is reissued. The Administrator checks the posting weekly.

Capacity: the Administrator compares the census to the license each day of admission activity. No admission is accepted if it would bring the census above licensed capacity. For an ACH, the Administrator also confirms that beds and services match the CON.

FCH only: the Administrator keeps the count of ambulatory and non-ambulatory residents within the license. The Administrator notifies ACLS if a resident's evacuation capability changes or if a non-resident will live in the home. If a resident becomes temporarily non-ambulatory, the Administrator notifies the DHSR Construction Section immediately and records the date and time of the call.
Ownership disclosure: on any new application the Administrator discloses all owners with a 5% or greater interest. The same ownership information is disclosed at each renewal.

Renewal: by October 1 each year, the Administrator starts the renewal for the next calendar year. It includes ownership disclosure, bed capacity (for an ACH, including any Alzheimer's special care unit) and census data (10A NCAC 13F .0208; 10A NCAC 13G .0208).

Renewal fee: the Administrator pays the nonrefundable renewal fee when invoiced by ACLS. The fee is $315 for a home with 6 or fewer beds, or $360 plus $17.50 per bed for a home with more than 6 beds (N.C.G.S. §131D-2.5). The Administrator confirms the amount with ACLS and records the payment date.

If a survey finds violations that remain uncorrected at renewal, ACLS may extend the plan of correction, issue a provisional license, or deny renewal. The Administrator tracks every plan of correction to completion (see GOV-04).

Change of licensee: at least 30 days before the effective date, the current licensee gives written notice to DHSR, the county DSS, and each resident or responsible person (10A NCAC 13F .0207; 10A NCAC 13G .0207). The Administrator keeps a copy of each notice with the date and method of delivery.

The prospective licensee files the change application, the fire and sanitation reports (each dated within 12 months) and the fee. The current licensee does not transfer the license. The new licensee must hold its own license.

Closing: at least 30 days before closing, the licensee gives written notice to DHSR, the county DSS, and each resident or responsible person. The notice states the closing date and the plan for moving residents (10A NCAC 13F .0211; 10A NCAC 13G .0211). The Administrator coordinates each resident's relocation under ADM-05 and returns funds under REF-01 and RR-02.

Notice of revocation: if the home receives a notice of revocation, the Administrator gives each resident and responsible person a written notice of the revocation and its basis within 5 calendar days (10A NCAC 13F .0212; 10A NCAC 13G .0212). The Administrator keeps a signed or dated delivery record for each recipient.

Appeals: the licensee may appeal a licensure action by filing a contested case under G.S. 150B-23, after attempts at informal resolution under G.S. 150B-22 (10A NCAC 13F .0213). The governing body decides whether to appeal and keeps all deadlines in the appeal file.

responsibilities.duty: Obtain the CON (ACH), hold the license, approve renewals, decide on appeals, and give the required notices for a change of licensee or a closing.
Prepare applications and renewals, post the license, keep census within capacity, notify ACLS and the Construction Section as required, and give the 5-day revocation notices.
Check the license posting and census at each shift handoff when the Administrator is absent and report any capacity concern immediately.
Check census and capacity before accepting any admission.

documentation: Current license and any provisional license with the DHSR notice of reasons
Application packets, CON documents (ACH), fee receipts and ACLS decision letters
Daily census record and capacity log
Renewal filings and ownership disclosure
Notices of change of licensee, closing and revocation with delivery records
Appeal file

policies.title: Policy Review, Document Control and ACLS Policy Approval
policies.applies_to: ACH and FCH
policies.purpose: To make sure the operational policies and procedures of [AGENCY NAME] are approved by ACLS before licensure, kept current, and followed by every staff member.
policies.policy: Licensure depends on ACLS approval of the operational policies and procedures (10A NCAC 13F .0204; 10A NCAC 13G .0204). For an FCH, the county adult home specialist reviews the operational plan first and then submits the packet to DHSR within 10 business days. This policy meets License a Family Care Home, Procedures step 2.b(vi) — Other policies and procedures of the home. All policies in this manual form part of the operational plan. Each policy carries a title, an ID, a version date and an approval signature. The Administrator reviews each policy at least annually, and again whenever a rule changes. Staff acknowledge in writing each policy and each revision.

definitions.definition: The written policies and procedures the home submits to ACLS for approval and follows in daily operation.
The date a policy was last approved, shown on the policy and recorded in the master index.
The county DSS staff member who reviews an FCH operational plan and submits the licensing packet to DHSR.

procedures: The Administrator keeps one master copy of the Policy & Procedure Manual and a master index showing each policy ID, title, version date, next review date and approval signature.
ACH: before the pre-licensing survey, the Administrator submits the complete policy manual to ACLS for approval, together with the application packet (10A NCAC 13F .0204).

FCH: the Administrator gives the manual to the county adult home specialist as part of the operational plan. The specialist reviews it and submits the packet to DHSR within 10 business days (10A NCAC 13G .0204). The Administrator records the date the manual was given to the county and the date the county reports submission.
The Administrator records every question or change request from ACLS or the county, the response, and the date revised policies were resubmitted.
No resident is admitted until the Administrator has written confirmation that ACLS has approved the policies and the license has been issued.

After approval, the Administrator signs and dates the cover page of each policy and places the approved set in a binder kept in the Administrator's office. A second copy is kept where all staff can reach it.

Annual review: each January, the Administrator reviews every policy against current rules, survey findings, incidents and grievances, and the quality assurance results (GOV-04). The review is recorded on the master index with the reviewer's initials and date.

Rule-change review: when DHSR, the Medical Care Commission or the General Assembly changes a rule or statute that affects the home, the Administrator reviews the affected policies within 30 days of the effective date. This includes the respite care rules that take effect July 1, 2026, which must be reflected in the admission, contract, staffing and care policies before the home offers respite stays.

When a policy is changed, the Administrator updates the version date, marks the change, and keeps the previous version in an archive file. The Administrator consults ACLS or the county adult home specialist before putting in place a change that alters how the home meets a licensing requirement.

Staff acknowledgment: each employee signs an acknowledgment form at hire and after each revision, naming the policies read. The Administrator trains staff on each change before it takes effect and records the training date.
The Administrator checks at least quarterly that posted notices, forms and staff practice match the current policies. Any mismatch is corrected within 14 days and logged.
Obsolete copies are removed from work areas on the day a revision takes effect.

responsibilities.duty: Adopt the policies, approve revisions and make sure resources exist to carry them out.
Submit policies to ACLS or the county, run the annual and rule-change reviews, keep the master index and archive, and obtain staff acknowledgments.
Make sure current policies are available to staff on each shift.
Read, acknowledge and follow current policies.

documentation: Master policy index with version and review dates
Approved policy manual with signatures
ACLS or county correspondence and approval letters
Archive of prior versions
Staff acknowledgment forms and training sign-in sheets
Annual review record

policies.title: Quality Assurance and Performance Improvement
policies.applies_to: ACH and FCH
policies.purpose: To find and correct problems in resident care and facility operations before they become violations, and to make sure every survey finding is corrected on time.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] runs a quality assurance and performance improvement (QAPI) program. At least quarterly, the Administrator reviews incidents, grievances, falls, medication errors and survey findings, identifies trends, and puts corrective actions in place. Every plan of correction is tracked until it is complete. The home understands that DHSR may impose administrative penalties for rule violations under N.C.G.S. §131D-34, and that penalties are listed publicly for the preceding 36 months. It also understands that violations left uncorrected can lead to a plan of correction extension, a provisional license or denial of renewal (10A NCAC 13F .0208; 10A NCAC 13G .0208). The county DSS monitors adult care facilities at least quarterly, and the home cooperates fully with that monitoring.

definitions.definition: The written plan the home submits to DHSR describing how and when each cited violation will be corrected.
A pattern of repeated events, such as several falls in the same location or repeated late medication passes.
The quarterly meeting and written summary in which management reviews quality data and assigns corrective actions.

procedures: The Administrator keeps running logs of incidents (INC-01), grievances (GRV-01), falls (HLT-05), medication errors (MED-02) and survey and monitoring findings.
Within 5 days after each calendar quarter ends, the Administrator compiles the counts and details from each log into one QAPI summary.

The Administrator holds a QAPI review each quarter with the designated manager, the infection control designee, the supervising nurse or contracted nurse (if any) and a governing body representative. The date and attendees are recorded.
The review looks for trends by resident, location, shift, day of week and staff member. It asks whether any rule requirement was missed, such as a report not filed or a notification not made.
For each problem found, the team writes a corrective action with a named responsible person and a due date no later than 30 days out unless a longer date is justified in writing.
The Administrator follows up on each corrective action at the next review and records whether it worked. If the problem continues, the action is revised.
Survey findings: within 1 business day of receiving a statement of deficiencies, the Administrator logs it and gives a copy to the governing body.
The Administrator prepares the plan of correction by the deadline stated in the DHSR notice, assigns an owner for each cited item, and submits the plan as directed.

The Administrator checks each correction in person, records the date of completion and the evidence (such as a corrected record, a repaired item or a training sign-in), and keeps it in the survey file.
If a correction cannot be completed by the plan date, the Administrator contacts ACLS before the date passes to ask for an extension and records the response.
The Administrator reviews county DSS quarterly monitoring reports the same way as survey findings and logs any recommendations and the home's response.
The Administrator checks the DHSR public penalty listing at least once a year and reviews any penalty against the home to find the cause and prevent it from recurring.
Before each annual renewal (GOV-02), the Administrator confirms that all cited violations have been corrected.
Staff are told about QAPI results and changes in practice at the next staff meeting, and the training date is recorded.

responsibilities.duty: Review the quarterly QAPI summary, provide resources for corrective actions, and hold the Administrator accountable for completion.
Compile data, lead the review, write and follow plans of correction, and respond to ACLS and the county.

responsibilities.role: Designated Manager and Infection Control Designee
responsibilities.duty: Take part in reviews, carry out assigned corrective actions and report new problems promptly.
Report incidents, errors and concerns promptly and take part in improvement training.

documentation: Quarterly QAPI summaries and meeting records
Incident, grievance, fall and medication error logs
Statements of deficiencies, plans of correction and completion evidence
County DSS monitoring reports
Records of ACLS contacts and extension requests
Staff training records on corrective actions

policies.title: Corporate Compliance, Billing Integrity and Special Assistance/Medicaid Rules
policies.applies_to: ACH and FCH
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] charges, bills and reports honestly, follows State/County Special Assistance (SA) and Medicaid rules, and avoids penalties and fee errors.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] bills and charges only for services actually provided and only in the amounts stated in the resident contract. A resident who receives State/County Special Assistance is charged no more than the SA maximum, and the facility must agree to accept the state rate. The resident keeps a $70 personal needs allowance, which the facility does not take for charges. SA room-and-board is funded 50% by the state and 50% by the county, and SA recipients are automatically Medicaid-eligible. New ACH beds approved by CON are certified for SA as described in the 2026 State Medical Facilities Plan, Policy LTC-3. The home does not bill NC Medicaid for personal care services, or use electronic visit verification (EVV), until it has confirmed with NC Medicaid whether and how those rules apply to the home. The home understands that DHSR may impose penalties under N.C.G.S. §131D-34 for rule violations and pays license fees as set by N.C.G.S. §131D-2.5.

definitions.definition: A state and county program that pays part of room and board for eligible residents of adult care homes and family care homes. The county DSS determines eligibility.
The $70 per month that an SA resident keeps for personal use. The facility may not charge it against room and board.

The highest monthly room-and-board amount the facility may charge an SA resident, set by the NC DHHS Division of Social Services. Different rates apply to the special care unit (dementia) and to enhanced maintenance.
The annual report to the NC DHHS Office of the Controller by facilities that serve SA residents or are exempt. The next report is due September 30, 2027.
Agreed-upon procedures engagement. It is no longer required for facilities with 7 or more beds beginning on or after July 1, 2026 (S.L. 2026-41).

procedures: The governing body adopts a code of conduct that bans false billing, kickbacks, double charging and misuse of resident funds. Each employee signs it at hire.

Before admitting an SA applicant, the Administrator tells the applicant and the county DSS in writing that the home accepts the current SA rate. The Administrator confirms the current SA maximum with the county DSS and the Division of Social Services each January and whenever the rate changes.

The Administrator makes sure no SA resident is charged above the SA maximum, including through extra fees, required deposits or required add-ons. Optional goods and services are offered only on a voluntary basis and billed only with the resident's written agreement.
The home does not take or hold the $70 personal needs allowance except under the written authorization and ledger process in RR-02.

The bookkeeper prepares monthly resident statements that match the contract in CON-01. The Administrator reviews a sample of statements each month against the contract and attendance (census and absence) records.

For any resident whose bed is certified for SA under the 2026 SMFP Policy LTC-3 (new CON beds), the Administrator confirms the certification terms with ACLS and the county and keeps a copy of the certification.

Before billing NC Medicaid for personal care services or using EVV, the Administrator asks NC Medicaid in writing whether the home may bill, under what code, and under what enrollment. The Administrator keeps the answer and does not bill until enrollment is confirmed in NCTracks.
The Administrator tracks the Adult Care Cost Report due date (September 30, 2027, then as notified), assigns the bookkeeper to prepare it by August 31, and signs it after review.
The Administrator confirms with the Office of the Controller whether an AUP is required for the home. For a facility with 7 or more beds that begins on or after July 1, 2026, the AUP is not required.
The home pays the annual license fee on time (see GOV-02), and the Administrator keeps the invoice and proof of payment.

Any employee who suspects a billing error or improper charge reports it to the Administrator, or to the governing body if the concern involves the Administrator. No one is punished for a good-faith report.
When an overbilling or overcharge is found, the Administrator corrects the account within 10 days, refunds the resident or payer in full, and logs the cause and the correction. Refunds follow REF-01.
The governing body reviews billing audit results, any DHSR penalties under N.C.G.S. §131D-34, and any payer inquiries at its quarterly QAPI review (GOV-04).

responsibilities.duty: Adopt the compliance code, review audit results and make sure the home meets SA and Medicaid conditions.
Confirm SA rates, review resident statements, prepare reports, make the Medicaid inquiry and correct billing errors.
Bill accurately, keep records, prepare statements and the cost report.
Follow the code of conduct and report suspected billing problems.

documentation: Signed code of conduct
SA rate confirmations, SA agreements and county DSS correspondence
Monthly resident statements and audit samples
SMFP LTC-3 certification records for new CON beds
NC Medicaid inquiry and response
Adult Care Cost Report and Office of the Controller correspondence
Refund and correction records

policies.title: Resident Rights and Responsibilities (Residents' Bill of Rights)
policies.applies_to: ACH and FCH
policies.purpose: To make sure every resident of [AGENCY NAME] knows and can use the rights guaranteed by North Carolina law, and that no staff member interferes with them.
policies.policy: This policy meets License a Family Care Home, Procedures step 2.b(ii) — Implementation of the family care home Residents' Bill of Rights. [AGENCY NAME] maintains every right in N.C.G.S. §131D-21 and makes sure residents can exercise those rights without hindrance (10A NCAC 13F .0909; 10A NCAC 13G .0909). Residents have the right to dignity and privacy; to a written statement of services and charges on admission; to be free of abuse, neglect and exploitation; to communicate privately; and to have phone access. Each resident gets a copy of G.S. 131D-21 on admission. A resident may be discharged only for the reasons in N.C.G.S. §131D-21(17), with at least 30 days' notice except when health or safety is in jeopardy, and may appeal and stay in the home until the appeal is resolved unless law provides otherwise.

definitions.definition: The rights listed in N.C.G.S. §131D-21, given to each resident in writing.

As defined in N.C.G.S. §131D-2.1. Abuse includes willful or grossly negligent infliction of pain, injury or mental anguish, unreasonable confinement, or deprivation of needed services by the administrator or staff.
A resident may use a right without being discouraged, punished, delayed or blocked by staff or by facility rules.
A person designated by the resident, or authorized by law, to act for the resident.

procedures: At or before admission, the Administrator or designee gives the resident and any responsible person a copy of N.C.G.S. §131D-21 and the home's written statement of services and charges (see CON-01). The resident or responsible person signs and dates the receipt, and a copy is placed in the resident record.
The person giving the rights reads or explains them in a manner the resident understands, using the language access steps in RR-05 when needed. The explanation is noted on the receipt.
The Administrator posts a copy of the Residents' Bill of Rights and the contact information for the Long-Term Care Ombudsman in a common area where residents and visitors can see them (see GRV-01).

Dignity and privacy: staff knock and wait before entering a resident's room, provide personal care in private, use the resident's preferred name, and discuss resident information only as RR-04 permits.

Communication: residents may send and receive mail unopened, have private visits (subject to VIS-01), and use a telephone in private. The Administrator keeps a phone available that residents may use at reasonable times without cost beyond what is stated in the contract.
Freedom from abuse, neglect and exploitation: staff follow INC-03. Any suspicion is reported at once to the Administrator and to the required authorities.

No staff member may restrict a right as punishment, for staff convenience or because a resident has filed a complaint. Any restriction that is medically required must be ordered by the physician, documented in the record and reviewed with the resident or responsible person.

Transfer and discharge: the Administrator follows ADM-05 and gives at least 30 days' written notice, except when the resident's presence puts health or safety at risk. The notice states the reason, the resident's appeal rights, and that the resident may stay in the home until an appeal is resolved unless law provides otherwise.
Complaints: any resident or responsible person may complain without fear of retaliation. The Administrator handles complaints under GRV-01.
Training: all staff are trained on resident rights at hire and at least once each year. Sign-in sheets and quiz or acknowledgment forms are kept in the personnel file.

Responsibilities of residents: the Administrator explains in plain terms that residents are asked to respect other residents and staff, follow the home's safety rules, pay charges as agreed in the contract, and tell staff about changes in health. These responsibilities never limit a legal right.

Each quarter, the Administrator checks that the rights are posted, that every record has a signed receipt, and that no complaints show a pattern of rights violations. Findings go to the QAPI review (GOV-04).
If a resident's right is found to have been violated, the Administrator acts within 24 hours to stop the violation, reports it as required, retrains staff involved, and records the action taken.

responsibilities.duty: Provide and explain rights, post notices, train staff, respond to violations and complaints.
Protect residents' rights on each shift and report any concern to the Administrator immediately.
Honor residents' rights, maintain privacy and dignity, and report suspected violations.
Ask questions, raise concerns, and follow the home's stated expectations.

documentation: Signed receipt for N.C.G.S. §131D-21 and the statement of services and charges
Posted rights and ombudsman notice (photo or checklist)
Staff training records on resident rights
Complaint and grievance log
Records of any physician-ordered restriction
Quarterly rights audit

policies.title: Resident Funds and Personal Property
policies.applies_to: ACH and FCH
policies.purpose: To protect residents' money and belongings from loss, misuse and exploitation, and to keep clear, auditable records of any funds the home holds.
policies.policy: Residents have the right to dignity, privacy and freedom from exploitation (N.C.G.S. §131D-21). Exploitation, as defined in N.C.G.S. §131D-2.1, includes misuse of a resident's money or property. [AGENCY NAME] never takes, borrows or uses a resident's money or property for any purpose other than that resident's benefit. The home holds funds only with the resident's or responsible person's written consent. Resident funds are kept completely separate from facility funds. A written receipt is given for every deposit and withdrawal, and a ledger is kept for each resident. Residents who receive Special Assistance keep their $70 personal needs allowance. Exploitation and misappropriation of resident property are reportable (see INC-03).

definitions.definition: Money, checks or benefits that belong to a resident and that the home holds, deposits or spends at the resident's request.
The $70 per month that a Special Assistance resident keeps for personal use.
Taking, using or keeping a resident's money or property without permission or legal right.
As defined in N.C.G.S. §131D-2.1, the improper use of a resident or the resident's resources for another person's profit or advantage.

procedures: At admission, the Administrator tells the resident and responsible person that the resident may keep, manage and control his or her own money and property. Holding funds is optional and is not a condition of admission.

If the resident or responsible person asks the home to hold funds, they sign a written consent form stating the purpose, the person who may make withdrawals, and how statements will be given. A copy goes in the resident record.

Funds held are kept in a locked box or safe in the Administrator's office, or in a separate bank account in the resident's name. They are never mixed with facility money, petty cash or another resident's funds.

For each deposit, the Administrator or designee counts the money with the person handing it over, issues a numbered written receipt, and enters it in the resident's ledger the same day. Two signatures are required.

For each withdrawal, the resident or authorized person signs the ledger. Staff keep the purchase receipt where a purchase is made for the resident and attach it to the ledger. Staff who handle funds are limited to those named by the Administrator.

The home does not accept gifts, loans or personal favors from residents, and no staff member may be named in a resident's will, power of attorney or account unless allowed by law and cleared with the Administrator and counsel.
The Administrator reconciles each ledger to the cash or bank balance every month and signs the reconciliation. A second person reviews it at least each quarter.
Residents or responsible persons receive a written statement at least quarterly and on request. They may inspect the ledger at any reasonable time.

Special Assistance residents: the home leaves the $70 personal needs allowance with the resident or deposits it in the ledger only if the resident has consented. The allowance is never applied to room and board or to other charges (see GOV-05).

Personal property: at admission, staff and the resident or responsible person list the resident's belongings on a signed inventory. Items brought in or removed later are added to the list with dates. The home advises residents to keep high-value items out of the home or arrange for secure storage.
Staff must not use residents' belongings, accept money for finding or fixing items, or enter a resident's belongings without permission except in an emergency or for a safety search under policy.

If money or property is missing, the resident or staff member tells the Administrator at once. The Administrator starts a search, interviews staff and the resident, and writes a report within 24 hours. If misappropriation or exploitation is suspected, the Administrator reports under INC-03 right away.
If the home is at fault for a loss, it replaces or repays the resident within 30 days and records the outcome.

At discharge or death, the Administrator reconciles the ledger, returns all funds and property with a signed receipt to the resident or the legally authorized person, and files the receipt (see HLT-08 and REF-01).
Staff are trained on this policy at hire and each year.

responsibilities.duty: Approve funds-holding consents, review ledgers, investigate losses and report suspected exploitation.
Handle deposits and withdrawals, issue receipts and maintain ledgers.
Respect residents' property, never take or borrow resident money, and report any loss or concern immediately.
Decide whether the home holds funds, review statements and sign for withdrawals.

documentation: Written consent to hold funds
Resident ledger and numbered receipts
Monthly reconciliations and quarterly reviews
Quarterly statements to residents
Personal property inventory
Loss investigation reports and INC-03 reports
Discharge or death property and fund receipts

policies.title: Advance Directives
policies.applies_to: Adult Care Homes (10A NCAC 13F) and Family Care Homes (10A NCAC 13G) — all administrators, managers, direct care staff and medication aides
policies.purpose: To make sure each resident's right to dignity, privacy and self-determination under N.C.G.S. §131D-21 is carried into health care decisions, by asking about advance directives at admission, filing them where staff can find them, and passing them on to hospice, EMS and hospital staff.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] asks every resident or resident representative about advance directives at admission and again at each reassessment and change of condition. We keep copies in the resident record and tell staff where they are filed. We honor documented wishes and give copies to hospice, EMS and the hospital whenever a resident receives outside care or is transferred. Having or not having an advance directive is never a condition of admission or continued residence, and it does not change the quality of care a resident receives. Staff do not give legal advice, do not complete directives for residents, and do not act as a resident's health care agent. This policy supports the resident's right to dignity and privacy and to a written statement of services (N.C.G.S. §131D-21; see RR-01 and CON-01).

definitions.definition: A written document in which a resident states health care wishes or names someone to decide when the resident cannot, such as a living will or health care power of attorney.

definitions.term: Do Not Resuscitate (DNR) order / Medical Orders for Scope of Treatment (MOST)
definitions.definition: Medical orders signed by an authorized physician or other authorized provider that direct emergency personnel on resuscitation and other treatment. They are different from the resident's own advance directive documents.
The person a resident has named in writing to make health care decisions if the resident cannot.
A legal guardian, health care agent or other person with legal authority to act for the resident.

procedures: At pre-admission and admission, the Administrator or designee asks the resident (or representative) whether the resident has a living will, health care power of attorney, DNR order, MOST form or other advance directive. The answer is recorded on the admission checklist the same day.
