When a resident falls, the nearest staff member stays with the resident, does not move the resident if a head, neck, back or hip injury is suspected, and calls the supervisor. Staff call 911 for any serious injury or if unsure; otherwise they perform only first aid they are trained to give.

After a fall, staff check the resident for injury and pain, and notify the physician and responsible person as directed in INC-01 and HLT-03. They document the time, place, circumstances, witnesses, condition and actions taken.
The staff member who found or responded to the fall completes the incident report before the end of the shift. Falls with injury are handled and reported as required by INC-01 and REC-02.

Within 24 hours of any fall, the Administrator or designee reassesses the resident's fall risk, determines the likely cause, and updates the care plan with new interventions. The resident and responsible person are told of the changes.

Staff monitor a resident who has fallen for changes in condition (new pain, confusion, bruising, drowsiness) for at least 72 hours, and document each check. Any concern is reported to the physician (HLT-03).
If a resident has had a significant change of condition or an injury that changes functional ability, the Administrator arranges a reassessment under 10A NCAC 13F .0801.
The Administrator reviews the falls log monthly for patterns by resident, time, place and cause, and brings trends to the quality assurance review (GOV-04).
Staff are trained on fall prevention, safe transfer, and post-fall response at orientation and annually (STF-03).

responsibilities.duty: Ensure screens and reassessments are completed on time, review the falls log monthly, correct environmental hazards, and report trends to QA.
Complete the resident assessment under 10A NCAC 13F .0801 and identify fall risk factors.
Follow care plan interventions, perform hazard checks, respond to falls, and document accurately.
Direct the response after a fall, ensure notifications are made, and complete the incident report review.
Review medications and evaluate residents after falls when requested.

documentation: Fall-risk screen at admission, annually and after each fall
DHSR assessment instrument or equivalent
Resident care plan with fall interventions and revision dates
Incident reports and post-fall monitoring notes
Physician and responsible person notification entries
Monthly falls log and QA review notes
Staff training records

policies.title: Skin Integrity
policies.applies_to: Adult Care Home (10A NCAC 13F) and Family Care Home (10A NCAC 13G); all residents, all direct care staff
policies.purpose: To protect residents' skin from breakdown, find skin problems early, and make sure pressure injuries and open areas are reported to a physician and treated.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] evaluates every resident's skin condition as part of the DHSR resident assessment instrument, which includes skin condition (10A NCAC 13G .0801, with the same content used in the ACH assessment). Skin checks and repositioning are written into the resident-centered care plan (10A NCAC 13F .0802), carried out as planned, and documented. Staff notify the physician of any pressure injury or open area. Treatments are provided only by staff who are legally permitted and trained to provide them, under physician orders and in accordance with HLT-02.

definitions.definition: Localized damage to skin or underlying tissue from pressure or pressure with shear, ranging from persistent redness to an open wound.
Any break in the skin, including a tear, blister, abrasion, rash with broken skin, or wound.
Changing a resident's body position at the interval written in the care plan to relieve pressure.
A visual inspection of the resident's skin, especially bony areas, heels, skin folds and under devices.

procedures: At admission, the person completing the pre-admission screening or admission notes any known skin conditions, wounds, or pressure injuries and records them in the resident record (ADM-01).
The qualified assessor completes the skin section of the DHSR assessment instrument within 30 days of admission, annually, and after a significant change of condition (ADM-02).

The care plan (ADM-03) states each resident's skin-risk level, the frequency of skin checks, repositioning schedule, pressure-relieving devices, continence care, nutrition and hydration needs, and any physician-ordered treatment.

Direct care staff check each resident's skin during bathing and dressing, and document findings at least [FREQUENCY, e.g., weekly] on the skin check form, with daily observation of bony areas for high-risk residents.
Staff reposition residents who cannot change position themselves at the interval written in the care plan, and record the time and initials each time.
Staff keep skin clean and dry, change soiled clothing and briefs promptly, use moisturizer as directed, and avoid dragging residents during transfers.
Staff encourage fluids and nutritious meals, and tell the supervisor if a resident is eating or drinking poorly (NUT-01).
If staff see new redness that does not fade, a blister, a break in skin, drainage, odor, or swelling, they report it to the supervisor immediately, before the end of the shift.

The supervisor looks at the area, documents the location, size, appearance, and any pain, and notifies the physician the same day for any pressure injury or open area (HLT-03). The responsible person is notified as well.
Treatments and dressing changes are performed only as ordered by the physician and only by staff who are authorized and trained, or by a nurse, home health or hospice agency (HLT-02, HLT-07).

The care plan is updated within 24 hours to include new physician orders, repositioning changes, and devices. The Administrator or designee reassesses the resident if there is a significant change of condition (ADM-02).
Staff reinforce positioning, offloading of heels, and keeping pressure off the area, and document that this was done.

If an injury does not improve, worsens, or shows signs of infection, the Administrator ensures the physician is contacted again and considers whether the resident's needs can still be met (HLT-03, ADM-04).
Staff use standard precautions when caring for open areas and dispose of dressings per INF-01 and INF-02.
The Administrator reviews all residents with skin problems monthly and brings trends to the quality assurance review (GOV-04).
Skin care and pressure-injury prevention are taught to staff at orientation and annually (STF-03).

responsibilities.duty: Ensure assessments, care plans and physician notifications are complete, monitor skin problems monthly, and arrange nursing support where needed.
Complete the skin section of the DHSR instrument accurately.
Check skin, reposition per care plan, document, and report changes immediately.
Examine and document reported areas, notify the physician and responsible person, and update orders.
Provide skilled wound care and teach staff under physician orders.

documentation: Skin section of the DHSR assessment instrument
Care plan with skin interventions and updates
Skin check forms and repositioning records
Physician notification and orders
Treatment records
Incident or change-of-condition notes
Monthly skin problem review and training records

policies.title: Hospice and Home Health Coordination
policies.applies_to: Adult Care Home (10A NCAC 13F) and Family Care Home (10A NCAC 13G); residents receiving hospice or home health services
policies.purpose: To make sure that residents who receive hospice or home health services get consistent, coordinated care, that responsibilities are clear, and that the care plan reflects the outside agency's orders.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] coordinates with licensed hospice and home health agencies so their orders and plans of care are consistent with the resident-centered care plan required by 10A NCAC 13F .0802. The facility documents which provider is responsible for which services. The facility reassesses the resident under 10A NCAC 13F .0801 after any significant change of condition, including a decline that leads to a hospice referral. The facility continues to provide the personal care, supervision, meals, medication assistance and other services it is licensed to provide, and does not allow an outside agency to replace its responsibilities. The facility continues to follow the limits on conditions it can serve (ADM-04).

definitions.definition: A licensed agency providing comfort-focused, end-of-life care to a resident under a physician's certification and a hospice plan of care.
A licensed agency providing skilled nursing, therapy or aide services to a resident in the home under physician orders.
The documented exchange of orders, plans, schedules and responsibilities among the facility, the outside agency, the physician and the resident or responsible person.
A major change in the resident's health or function that requires reassessment under the assessment rule.

procedures: When a physician orders hospice or home health, or when a resident or responsible person requests it, the Administrator or designee is informed and records the request in the resident record.
The Administrator confirms that the agency is licensed and that the resident or responsible person has chosen it, and records the agency name, contact numbers and after-hours number.
Before services start, the Administrator or designee obtains a copy of the physician's order and the agency's plan of care, and asks for a named agency contact (nurse or case manager).

The Administrator or designee meets (in person or by phone) with the agency and the resident or responsible person within [TIMEFRAME, e.g., 2 business days] of the first agency visit to agree on who will provide which services.

The facility records the division of responsibilities on a coordination form for each resident, listing the facility's duties (such as personal care, meals, medication assistance, supervision) and the agency's duties (such as skilled care, therapy, bathing aide visits, comfort care).

Within 48 hours of receiving the agency plan, the Administrator or designee reassesses the resident under 10A NCAC 13F .0801 because the resident has had a significant change, and updates the care plan under 10A NCAC 13F .0802 so that agency orders and facility interventions fit together.
A copy of the current care plan, agency plan, and orders is kept where staff can access it, and staff are told of changes at shift change.

Medication orders from the agency are given to the Administrator and handled according to MED-01 and MED-02. Staff do not follow verbal agency instructions without confirming them with the supervisor and documenting them.
Agency staff sign in and out at each visit, and their visit notes or communication logs are placed in or alongside the resident record where the agency permits it.
Facility staff report changes in condition to both the physician or agency (as directed in the plan) and the responsible person (HLT-03).
Staff follow the hospice plan for comfort measures, and the facility stays in contact with the hospice team about pain, breathing, eating and other symptoms.
If the resident's needs exceed what the facility can provide even with agency support, the Administrator reviews ADM-04 and, if necessary, starts the discharge process in ADM-05.
If the resident is discharged from hospice or home health, the Administrator reassesses the resident and updates the care plan.
When a resident dies while receiving hospice, staff follow HLT-08, including notifying the hospice.
The Administrator reviews coordination for all residents receiving outside services quarterly and brings concerns to QA (GOV-04).

responsibilities.duty: Verify the agency, convene coordination, assure reassessment and care plan updates, and resolve problems with the agency.
Reassess the resident after a significant change of condition.
Follow the coordinated care plan, record observations, and report changes to the supervisor.
Communicate with agency staff, confirm orders, and notify the physician and responsible person.
Provide services under its plan of care and keep the facility informed of changes.

documentation: Physician order and agency plan of care
Agency contact information
Coordination of services form showing who provides which services
Reassessment and updated care plan
Agency visit logs or notes
Notifications to the physician and responsible person
Quarterly coordination review

policies.title: Death of a Resident
policies.applies_to: Adult Care Home (10A NCAC 13F) and Family Care Home (10A NCAC 13G); all staff
policies.purpose: To make sure a resident's death is handled with dignity and respect for family wishes, that the right people are notified promptly, that the circumstances are documented, and that belongings, funds and records are handled lawfully.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] treats the death of a resident with respect and notifies the physician, the responsible person and, if applicable, the hospice agency promptly. Staff document the time and circumstances of the death. Unexpected deaths are reported and handled as required by INC-01 and REC-02. Residents' personal property and funds are released according to RR-02 and refunds and deposits according to REF-01. The Administrator confirms current statutory and rule requirements and timelines under G.S. Chapter 131D and the Adult Care Licensure Section's rules before finalizing any report, release, or refund, and records the confirmation in the file. The resident's advance directive and funeral wishes are followed where known (RR-03).

definitions.definition: A death that is anticipated due to a known terminal illness, usually while the resident is receiving hospice care and has a do-not-resuscitate order.
A sudden or unanticipated death, a death after an accident or incident, or a death with unclear cause, including any suspicious circumstance.
The resident's legal representative, family member or other person identified in the resident record as the contact for decisions and notifications.
The resident's clothing, belongings, valuables and funds held by the facility.

procedures: If a resident is found unresponsive, staff immediately call the supervisor and check the resident's advance directive or DNR order (RR-03). Staff trained in CPR begin CPR unless a valid order says not to, and call 911 as appropriate.

When death occurs or is discovered, the staff member on duty notes the time, location, who found the resident, the resident's position and condition, and any actions taken, and informs the Administrator or manager on call immediately.
The Administrator or manager on call notifies the resident's physician right away, and records the name of the person notified and the time.

The Administrator or manager on call notifies the responsible person as soon as possible, in person or by phone, with compassion, and records the time and the person's name. If the person cannot be reached, staff try the next contact on file and document each attempt.
If the resident was receiving hospice, the hospice agency is called immediately and directs pronouncement and release procedures (HLT-07).

If the death was unexpected, or occurred after a fall, injury, abuse, neglect or any suspicious circumstance, the Administrator calls 911 or law enforcement as appropriate, does not disturb the scene, and follows INC-01 and INC-03. The Administrator notifies the medical examiner when required.
Staff treat the resident's body with dignity, keep the room private, and keep other residents' exposure to a minimum. They do not remove equipment or devices if an investigation is required.

When the physician, hospice or medical examiner has authorized release, the Administrator contacts the funeral home chosen by the resident or family, and documents the time of release and the staff present.
The Administrator notifies the county Department of Social Services if the resident received Special Assistance, and any other payor, agency or representative payee as needed (GOV-05).

The Administrator submits required reports to the state as described in INC-01 and REC-02, within the timelines the Administrator has confirmed under the applicable rule, and records the date and method sent.
Staff inventory the resident's belongings and any funds held in the presence of a second staff member, and secure them in a locked area (RR-02).
The Administrator releases belongings and funds to the legal representative or estate according to RR-02 and the written agreement in CON-01, obtains a signed receipt, and keeps a copy in the record.
The Administrator calculates and issues any refund of unused fees or deposits according to REF-01, and documents the amount, date and recipient.
Medications of the deceased resident are removed from the active supply and disposed of according to MED-02, with a second staff member witnessing and documenting.
The Administrator completes a death note in the resident record that includes the date and time, circumstances, notifications made (with times), disposition of the body, and release of belongings.
Staff clean the room according to infection control procedures (INF-03) and the bed is not reassigned until the room is ready.
The Administrator offers to let staff and residents who knew the resident to receive support and, where the family agrees, to share in a remembrance.
The Administrator reviews each death at the next quality assurance meeting for lessons learned (GOV-04), and retains the record according to REC-01.

responsibilities.duty: Direct the response, notify required parties, confirm reporting and release timelines, release belongings, issue refunds and complete the record.
Respond immediately, begin notifications, protect the scene if the death is unexpected, and document.
Call for help, perform CPR where required and permitted, care for other residents, and document what they observed.
Pronounce death and authorize release of the body.

documentation: Death note in the resident record with times and circumstances
Notification log (physician, responsible person, hospice, DSS, funeral home)
Incident report and state report where required
Inventory and signed receipt for belongings and funds
Refund calculation and record of payment
Medication disposal record
Record of confirmation of applicable timelines
QA review note

policies.title: Housekeeping, Laundry and Maintenance
policies.applies_to: Adult Care Home (10A NCAC 13F) and Family Care Home (10A NCAC 13G); housekeeping, laundry, maintenance and direct care staff
policies.purpose: To keep the building, equipment, furnishings, grounds and laundry clean, safe, functional and in good repair so residents live in a safe and comfortable environment.
policies.policy: This policy addresses item FCH-2.b(iv), the services and accommodation requirements, of the licensing procedures (License a Family Care Home, step 2.b). [AGENCY NAME] keeps walls, ceilings and floors clean, safe and functional, and prevents persistent unpleasant odors (10A NCAC 13F .0306). Heating, mechanical, plumbing and fire safety equipment is maintained in safe operating condition (10A NCAC 13F .0306). Outside premises are kept clean and safe (10A NCAC 13F .0306). The fire alarm system transmits automatically to the local fire department dispatch center, directly or through a third-party monitoring service, and the facility complies with local ordinances and city and county fire safety requirements (10A NCAC 13F .0307). New construction, additions, alterations and repairs meet the physical plant requirements in 10A NCAC 13F .0300; existing facilities meet the code in effect when licensed or altered, and equivalencies are requested from DHSR where needed (10A NCAC 13F .0301). Family Care Homes also meet the corresponding 13G physical plant requirements. Laundry and sanitation follow infection control procedures in INF-03.

definitions.definition: Routine cleaning of resident rooms, bathrooms, common areas, kitchens and outdoor areas.
Scheduled inspection, testing and servicing of building systems and equipment to prevent failure.
Any construction, addition, renovation or repair that changes the building or its systems and that requires review under the physical plant rules.
A service that receives the facility's alarm signal and forwards it to the local fire department dispatch center.

procedures: The Administrator assigns housekeeping, laundry and maintenance duties in writing and posts the cleaning schedule, listing each task, area, frequency and the person responsible.
Housekeeping staff clean resident rooms, bathrooms, dining and common areas daily, and clean floors, walls and ceilings so that they remain clean, safe and functional.

Staff report persistent unpleasant odors, stains, leaks or damaged surfaces to the Administrator the same day. The Administrator identifies the cause (for example continence care, plumbing, or ventilation) and corrects it.

The maintenance person or designee completes a monthly walk-through of the interior and exterior using a written checklist covering floors, walls, ceilings, lighting, handrails, grab bars, doors, windows, furniture, and any hazards.

The maintenance person tests and services heating, ventilation, plumbing, water heater temperatures, mechanical and electrical equipment, and fire safety equipment on a schedule set by the manufacturer, local code and FIR-01, and records the date and results.

The Administrator confirms that the fire alarm system transmits automatically to the local fire department dispatch center, directly or through a third-party service, and keeps the monitoring contract or documentation. The Administrator ensures the system is tested and any trouble signal is corrected right away, as required by FIR-01.
The Administrator checks local city and county fire safety ordinances annually and schedules inspections and corrections.

Outside areas, including walkways, entrances, parking, porches, ramps and yards, are inspected weekly and kept clean, free of debris, and safe from slip and trip hazards (snow, ice, leaves, holes). Staff correct hazards promptly or block off the area.

Any repair that is an addition, alteration or renovation is reviewed in advance by the Administrator. Before work begins, the Administrator confirms that plans meet 13F .0300 (or the equivalent 13G requirements for a Family Care Home) and contacts the DHSR Construction Section at 919-855-3893 for plan review where required, and keeps the approval on file (10A NCAC 13F .0301).

Maintenance requests are written on a work-order log with the date, problem, person reporting, priority, date completed and person completing. Urgent hazards (no heat, no water, electrical hazards, broken exits) are fixed immediately or the area is closed and residents moved if necessary.
Laundry staff collect soiled linens and clothing in closed containers, handle them with gloves using standard precautions (INF-01), and keep soiled and clean laundry separate.

Linens are washed in hot water with detergent and dried completely, and clean laundry is stored in a clean, covered area. Residents' clothing is labeled and returned to the correct resident, and any lost or damaged clothing is reported to the Administrator and documented (RR-02).
Housekeeping and laundry staff store cleaning chemicals in a locked or restricted area away from food and medications, and keep safety data sheets available.
Residents may keep their rooms as they wish within safety limits, and staff respect residents' privacy when cleaning (RR-01).
Housekeeping, laundry and maintenance staff are trained at orientation and annually on cleaning methods, chemical safety, infection control and incident reporting (STF-03).
The Administrator reviews the work-order log and inspection results monthly and brings repeated or unresolved problems to the quality assurance review (GOV-04).

responsibilities.duty: Assign duties, ensure systems are maintained and alarm monitoring is in place, approve alterations, and review logs monthly.
Perform inspections and repairs, test equipment, keep the work-order log, and report urgent hazards.
Perform scheduled cleaning and laundry procedures using standard precautions, and report problems.
Keep resident areas tidy, report hazards, odors and damage, and protect residents' clothing and belongings.

documentation: Cleaning schedule and housekeeping logs
Monthly interior/exterior inspection checklists
Work-order and repair log
Equipment testing and servicing records
Fire alarm monitoring contract or documentation
Construction plan approvals, equivalency requests and DHSR correspondence
Training records
Monthly QA review notes

policies.title: Transportation
policies.applies_to: Adult Care Home (10A NCAC 13F) and Family Care Home (10A NCAC 13G); all staff who drive or arrange transportation for residents
policies.purpose: To make sure residents can get to medical appointments, outings and other activities safely, that vehicles and drivers meet safety and insurance standards, and that residents are transported safely in an emergency evacuation.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] arranges or provides transportation for residents to medical appointments and, as staffing allows, to activities and outings, according to each resident's care plan and the resident contract. All vehicles used to transport residents are insured, maintained and inspected. Drivers are qualified and trained. Residents are secured with seatbelts, and wheelchairs are secured with approved securement systems. Transportation for emergency evacuation is arranged in the disaster plan (FIR-02). Any charge for transportation is disclosed in the resident contract (CON-01). If a resident is injured or becomes ill during transportation, staff follow INC-01 and HLT-03.

definitions.definition: A vehicle owned or leased by [AGENCY NAME] and used to transport residents.
A staff member approved by the Administrator after verification of a valid license, driving record and training.
Use of seatbelts and approved wheelchair tie-down and occupant restraint systems to keep a resident safe in a moving vehicle.
A staff member or designated person who accompanies a resident to an appointment or outing.

procedures: At admission, the Administrator or designee asks each resident and responsible person about transportation needs, including regular medical appointments, and records them in the care plan (ADM-03).

Transportation fees, mileage charges and any arrangements for family or third-party transportation are described in the resident contract (CON-01) before admission, and any change is given in writing.

Medical appointments are scheduled on the appointment calendar, with the date, time, location, physician, reason, transportation method and escort. The responsible staff member prepares the resident's medication list, orders, and face sheet for the visit.

The Administrator approves each driver in writing after checking that the driver holds a valid driver's license for the vehicle type, has an acceptable driving record, completes the required background checks (STF-02), and completes training on safe transport, securement, and emergency response (STF-03).
The Administrator keeps copies of each driver's license and re-verifies it at least annually and whenever the staff member reports a change or violation.
The Administrator confirms that each facility vehicle is registered, inspected as required by law, and covered by auto liability insurance. Proof of insurance is kept on file and in the vehicle.

The assigned driver or the maintenance person inspects each facility vehicle before use for tires, brakes, lights, mirrors, seatbelts, wheelchair lift and tie-downs, fluids, and cleanliness, and records the check on the vehicle log. Vehicles with a safety defect are not used until repaired.
Vehicles are maintained according to the manufacturer's schedule and any repairs are recorded in the vehicle maintenance log.

Before leaving, the driver verifies the resident list, checks that each resident is wearing a seatbelt, and secures wheelchairs with the approved tie-down and occupant restraint system. Residents do not ride in wheelchairs that are not rated for transport without securement.
Staff assist residents with boarding and exiting, use the lift or ramp correctly, and never leave a resident alone in a vehicle.
The driver carries the facility phone, a first-aid kit, and emergency contacts. Staff do not use handheld phones while driving.

The number of staff escorting residents is determined by the residents' needs and supervision requirements in the care plan, so that residents who need supervision are not left unattended (HLT-01, STF-01). Staffing at the facility is not reduced below required levels while staff are away (STF-01).
Residents are signed out and in according to VIS-01, with the time, destination, escort and expected return.

If a resident becomes ill or is injured while being transported, the driver pulls over safely, calls 911 if needed, notifies the Administrator, and records the event. Reporting follows INC-01 and HLT-03.
If a resident is missing from an outing, staff follow MIS-01 immediately.
If a vehicle accident occurs, staff call 911, care for residents first, notify the Administrator, the responsible persons, and the insurance carrier, and complete an incident report (INC-01).

Transportation needed for evacuation, including accessible vehicles and the number of residents who need assistance, is identified in the disaster plan and agreements with transport providers are kept on file (FIR-02).

When a resident uses a family member, public or contracted transport provider, the Administrator confirms the pickup arrangement, shares needed medical information, and documents the hand-off and return.
The Administrator reviews vehicle logs, driver files and transportation incidents at least quarterly and brings findings to the quality assurance review (GOV-04).

responsibilities.duty: Approve drivers, ensure vehicle insurance and maintenance, set escort levels, and review logs and incidents.
Hold a valid license, inspect the vehicle, secure residents, drive safely, and report problems or incidents.
Accompany the resident, carry needed documents and medications, and report outcomes to the Administrator.
Service vehicles and lifts, and keep maintenance records.
Prepare residents for trips, update the appointment calendar and sign-out log, and communicate changes in condition.

documentation: Appointment calendar and transportation requests
Driver approval, license copies and training records
Vehicle registration, inspection and insurance records
Vehicle inspection and maintenance logs
Resident sign-out and return log
Incident reports and accident reports
Transportation agreements for evacuation
Quarterly transportation review

policies.title: Staffing Levels and Supervision
policies.applies_to: ACH and FCH
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] always has enough qualified, trained staff on every shift to provide personal care and supervision to every resident, and to meet the North Carolina staffing thresholds for the home's licensed size and census.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] schedules staff by shift and by current census, never by licensed capacity alone. Shifts are the State-defined shifts: 1st shift 7:01 a.m.–3:00 p.m., 2nd shift 3:01 p.m.–11:00 p.m., and 3rd shift 11:01 p.m.–7:00 a.m. (10A NCAC 13F .0102). In a home with 7 to 20 residents, at least one designated staff member is on duty each shift to provide personal care and supervision. In a home with 7 to 12 residents, the administrator or manager is on site or within 500 feet with two-way communication, and an awake staff member is on duty whenever any resident is disoriented or wanders. For a census of 21 to 40, at least 16 aide duty hours are provided on both the 1st and 2nd shifts (10A NCAC 13F .0608). When the census reaches 31 or more, a Personal Care Aide Supervisor is designated. When the census reaches 81 or more, the administrator is on duty 8 hours a day, 5 days a week. At least one staff person on the premises at all times has completed a CPR and choking-management course within the last 24 months. This is an agency requirement for every shift, including nights, weekends and holidays. Staffing for a licensed Family Care Home (10A NCAC 13G) is confirmed with ACLS before the schedule is set, because the family care home staffing rules were not retrieved when this manual was prepared. No staffing arrangement may fall below what the rules require for the current census. No resident is left unsupervised in a way that puts the resident's health or safety at risk.

definitions.definition: Time a staff member spends providing direct personal care and supervision to residents, as defined in 10A NCC 13F .0102. Administrative, cooking, housekeeping and similar time is not counted unless the rule allows it.
The total hours of aide duty provided on a shift, used to measure compliance in homes of 21 to 40 residents.
A person designated in writing who is responsible for the day-to-day operation of the home in the administrator's absence (10A NCAC 13F .0102 and Rule .0402).
The staff member designated to supervise personal care aides in a home with a census of 31 or more (10A NCAC 13F .0102 and Rule .0609).
A person who is available by telephone or other means and able to reach the home within the time the rules and this policy require, but who is not counted as on-duty staff.
Awareness of a resident's general whereabouts and condition, with staff available to give the assistance the resident's care plan requires.
1st shift 7:01 a.m.–3:00 p.m.; 2nd shift 3:01 p.m.–11:00 p.m.; 3rd shift 11:01 p.m.–7:00 a.m.

procedures: The Administrator records the daily census each morning on the census log, and recalculates the required staffing whenever the census changes by admission, discharge or death.

The Administrator keeps a one-page staffing requirements chart at the front of the staffing schedule. It lists each census band, the minimum designated staff per shift, the aide duty hours required, and when a Personal Care Aide Supervisor or administrator on-duty hours apply.
For a 7–20 resident home, the Administrator schedules at least one designated staff member for personal care and supervision on every shift, and names that person on the schedule.

For a 7–12 resident home, the Administrator schedules coverage so that the administrator or manager is on site or within 500 feet with working two-way communication (for example, a charged cell phone or intercom). The Administrator tests this at least monthly and documents the test.

The Administrator marks on the schedule which shifts require an awake staff member because a resident is disoriented or wanders (see WAN-01 and HLT-04), and updates the marking whenever an assessment or change of condition identifies such a resident.

For a 21–40 resident home, the Administrator totals the scheduled aide duty hours for 1st and 2nd shifts each week and confirms that at least 16 hours are scheduled on each of those shifts. Administrative and other non-care time is not counted toward the total.

When the census reaches 31 or more, the Administrator designates a qualified Personal Care Aide Supervisor in writing, and documents the designation in the personnel file before the 31st resident is admitted.
When the census reaches 81 or more, the Administrator schedules their own on-duty time at 8 hours a day, 5 days a week, and documents it on the schedule.

The Administrator confirms the current staffing requirement for any census not listed in this policy, and for Family Care Home (13G) staffing, by contacting ACLS at 919-855-3765 or DHSR.AdultCare.Questions@dhhs.nc.gov before the schedule is posted. The Administrator keeps the written answer on file.

The Administrator names on every posted schedule at least one staff person on the premises who has a current CPR and choking-management certificate (completed within the last 24 months). The Administrator checks the schedule for this coverage before posting it and corrects any gap.

The Administrator posts the schedule where staff can see it. It shows names, shift, hours, the designated staff member, the manager on duty and the on-call person for the week. Changes are made in writing and initialed by the Administrator or manager.

If a staff member calls out, the person in charge calls the on-call list in this order: [ON-CALL LIST ORDER]. The Administrator or manager covers the shift if no replacement is found. The shift is never left below the minimum, and the shortage and fix are documented.

At each shift change, the outgoing designated staff member gives the incoming one a verbal and written report on residents' conditions, incidents, missing medications, residents who wander and anything needing follow-up. The report is documented on the shift report log.

The Administrator keeps time sheets or time-clock records and compares them with the schedule each pay period to confirm that scheduled coverage was actually provided. Variances are explained in writing.

Each month the Administrator reviews staffing as part of the quality assurance review (see GOV-04). The review looks at call-outs, shifts that came close to the minimum, resident falls or incidents by shift, and any resident whose needs call for added staff.
The Administrator keeps schedules, time records and the staffing requirements chart for the time required under REC-01 and makes them available to ACLS and county DSS on request.

responsibilities.duty: Determines required staffing from the census, builds and approves schedules, confirms CPR/choking coverage, designates the Personal Care Aide Supervisor, confirms unclear requirements with ACLS and documents compliance.
Carries out this policy in the Administrator's absence, handles call-outs and staffing shortfalls, and notifies the Administrator of any shift that cannot be covered.
When designated at a census of 31 or more, directs and checks the work of aides on assigned shifts and reports staffing or care problems to the Administrator.
Provides personal care and supervision on the assigned shift, stays on the premises, completes the shift report and does not leave residents unsupervised.

documentation: Daily census log
Staffing requirements chart
Posted weekly schedules and changes
Time sheets/time-clock records
Shift report log
CPR/choking course certificates for staff
Personal Care Aide Supervisor designation
Two-way communication tests (7–12 resident homes)
Written confirmations from ACLS on staffing questions
Monthly staffing review notes

policies.title: Background Checks, Employee Registries and Personnel Records
policies.applies_to: ACH and FCH
policies.purpose: To make sure that [AGENCY NAME] screens administrators and staff before they have resident contact, checks the required employee registries, and keeps a complete and confidential personnel file for every employee.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] does not allow any person to work alone with residents until the required screening is complete. Administrator applicants must have a criminal background check as part of certification or approval (G.S. 90-288.14 for adult care home administrators; 10A NCAC 13G .1501 for family care home administrators). The State Bureau of Investigation check costs $14, or $38 when an FBI check is included. State results usually take about two weeks, and FBI results can take up to 12 weeks, so applicants must request the check early. The Health Care Personnel Registry is checked before any hire, and findings are handled as set out in INC-03. Other background check requirements for staff and owners beyond the administrator were not verified when this manual was prepared. The Administrator therefore confirms the current requirements with ACLS (919-855-3765) before the first hire and again at each annual policy review. As agency practice, [AGENCY NAME] also obtains a criminal history check on every employee before the employee has unsupervised contact with residents, and does not hire a person whose check or registry result shows a disqualifying finding. A personnel file is kept for every employee, whether full time, part time, contract or temporary.

definitions.definition: The State registry of health care personnel with substantiated findings of abuse, neglect, exploitation, misappropriation of resident property or similar findings, which must be checked before hire.
A North Carolina State Bureau of Investigation criminal record check ($14).
A national fingerprint-based criminal record check, obtained together with the SBI check for $38.
The confidential file kept for each employee, containing hiring, screening, training, health and performance records.
Working with a resident when another screened and trained staff member is not present.

procedures: Before offering a job, the Administrator or designee has the applicant complete the application, including work history, references and a signed consent for the criminal background check and registry checks.
The Administrator checks the Health Care Personnel Registry for every applicant before the first day of work and prints or saves the result with the date and the name of the person who checked.
If the registry shows a substantiated finding, the Administrator does not hire the person and documents the reason without disclosing it to anyone who does not need to know.

The Administrator requests a criminal history check on every employee and has it completed before the employee has unsupervised resident contact. The employee does not provide care alone until the Administrator has reviewed and documented the result.

The Administrator confirms with ACLS the current rules on staff and owner background checks before the first hire, records the answer and date in the personnel policy file, and re-confirms it at each annual policy review (GOV-03).

For an administrator or manager applicant, the Administrator ensures the SBI check ($14) or the SBI/FBI check ($38) is requested at the start of the certification or approval process. This allows for about 2 weeks for State results and up to 12 weeks for FBI results.

The Administrator reviews every criminal history result within 3 business days of receipt, decides, and documents the decision with the date and signature. Any conviction is evaluated against the duties of the job and the safety of residents.
The Administrator checks that the applicant's licenses, certificates and training (for example CPR, nurse licensure or medication aide status) are valid and copies them to the file.

The Administrator keeps a personnel file for every employee that includes: application and resume, references, background and registry results, job description, signed orientation checklist, training records, TB screening (INF-05), signed confidentiality and conduct acknowledgments, performance reviews and discipline.

The Administrator keeps personnel files in a locked cabinet or access-controlled electronic system. Only the Administrator, manager and persons authorized by law, including ACLS and county DSS, may see them.
The Administrator checks the Health Care Personnel Registry for every current employee at least [REGISTRY RECHECK INTERVAL] and whenever an allegation is received, and documents each check.

When an allegation of abuse, neglect, exploitation or misappropriation involves an employee, the Administrator follows INC-03 for reporting to the State. The employee is removed from resident contact during the investigation.
The Administrator maintains a roster of all employees showing hire date, position, screening dates, CPR expiration and training due dates, and updates it monthly.
When an employee leaves, the Administrator documents the date and reason, collects keys and access, and keeps the file for the retention period set out in REC-01.

responsibilities.duty: Ensures screening is done before resident contact, checks the registry, makes and documents hiring decisions, confirms current requirements with ACLS and safeguards the files.
Does not allow any unscreened person to work alone with residents when the Administrator is absent and notifies the Administrator of any concern.
Provides truthful information, consents to checks, and reports any new arrest or charge to the Administrator within [REPORTING TIMEFRAME].

documentation: Employment application and signed consents
Health Care Personnel Registry check results
Criminal history results and hiring decision memos
SBI/FBI check receipts for administrator applicants
Written confirmation from ACLS of background check requirements
Personnel file index and employee roster
Registry recheck log

policies.title: Hiring, Orientation and Ongoing Training
policies.applies_to: ACH and FCH
policies.purpose: To make sure that every person hired by [AGENCY NAME] is oriented before working with residents and keeps the required training current, including CPR and choking training, medication aide training where applicable, and manager continuing education.
policies.policy: No employee works unsupervised with residents until orientation is complete and documented. Staff who administer medications at an adult care home, and their direct supervisors, must complete the required training and clinical skills validation and pass the written examination required by G.S. 131D-4.5B. Persons whose occupational licensure law authorizes them to administer medications are exempt from this requirement but must still be authorized under MED-01. At least one staff person on the premises at all times holds a CPR and choking-management certificate completed within the last 24 months (10A NCAC 13F). The manager designated under STF-05 must complete 12 continuing education hours each year (ACLS staffing rules effective 9/1/2024). All employees receive and document orientation, infection control training and abuse prevention training. The Administrator keeps a training matrix and checks the current ACLS training requirements and ACLS-approved curricula before each hire and annually, since required hours vary by position and are not set out in this policy.

definitions.definition: Instruction given before unsupervised work covering the home, residents' rights, emergency procedures and the employee's duties.
A staff member who has completed the training, clinical skills validation and written exam required by G.S. 131D-4.5B and who is authorized to give medications.
Direct observation and sign-off by a qualified person that the staff member can correctly perform medication administration tasks.
Training hours completed each year to maintain skills and meet the rules, including 12 hours a year for managers.
A chart listing each employee, required training, completion dates and due dates.

procedures: The Administrator or designee verifies the job requirements, credentials and screening (STF-02) for every applicant before a hire is made.

On or before the first shift, the new employee receives and signs for a copy of the job description, this Policy and Procedure Manual sections that apply to the job, the residents' rights (RR-01) and the abuse reporting duty (INC-03).

Before working unsupervised, the employee completes orientation covering the home layout, fire evacuation plan and drill roles (FIR-01), disaster plan (FIR-02), resident rights, confidentiality (RR-04), incident reporting (INC-01), missing resident search (MIS-01), wandering (WAN-01) and the employee's assigned tasks.

Before working unsupervised, the employee receives infection control training that includes standard precautions, hand hygiene, glove use and bloodborne pathogens (INF-01, INF-02), and abuse, neglect and exploitation prevention training (INC-03). Both are recorded on the orientation checklist with date and trainer signature.

For the first [SHADOWING PERIOD] the new employee works alongside an experienced, trained staff member. The trainer signs off on each competency (for example transfers, bathing, feeding, toileting) after observing it.

The Administrator confirms that each employee who will give medications is either a person exempt under G.S. 131D-4.5B or has completed the training, clinical skills validation and written exam. The Administrator keeps copies of the proof in the personnel file. No staff member gives medications until this is verified and the authorization in MED-01 is documented.
The Administrator likewise ensures each direct supervisor of medication staff has completed the same requirements.
The Administrator verifies CPR and choking-management certificates for each employee and enters the expiration date in the training matrix. Renewal is scheduled before the 24-month limit.

The Administrator checks the staff schedule each week to make sure that at least one person with a current CPR/choking certificate is on the premises on every shift, and arranges additional certification when coverage is short.
The designated manager's 12 CE hours per year are tracked in the training matrix. The Administrator keeps certificates and does not count the same hours twice.
The Administrator reviews the ACLS training page each January for changes in required training and updates the matrix and the annual training calendar.

The Administrator schedules in-service training at least [IN-SERVICE FREQUENCY] on topics including infection control, abuse prevention, fall prevention, dementia care and emergency procedures. Staff sign an attendance sheet.

The Administrator reviews the training matrix monthly. Employees with training due within 60 days are notified in writing, and an employee with expired required training is removed from the affected duty until training is complete.
The Administrator evaluates each new employee's performance at the end of the probationary period and annually, documents the evaluation and addresses training needs.
All orientation records, certificates, in-service sign-in sheets and the training matrix are kept in the personnel file or training binder and made available to ACLS and county DSS on request.

responsibilities.duty: Ensures orientation and training are completed and documented, verifies medication aide status and CPR coverage, maintains the training matrix and plans in-service training.
Completes 12 CE hours each year, assists with orientation and shadowing and enforces the training restrictions in the Administrator's absence.
Teaches and observes new employees, signs off competencies only when they are demonstrated, and reports concerns.
Completes required training on time, keeps certificates current and gives copies to the Administrator.

documentation: Signed orientation checklist
Training matrix
CPR/choking-management certificates
Medication aide training, skills validation and exam records or proof of licensure exemption
Manager CE certificates
In-service sign-in sheets and topics
Competency sign-off forms
Performance evaluations

policies.title: Staff Conduct and Professional Boundaries
policies.applies_to: ACH and FCH
policies.purpose: To set the standards of conduct that protect residents' dignity, privacy, property and safety, to prevent abuse, neglect and exploitation, and to state the consequences of violations.
policies.policy: Staff of [AGENCY NAME] treat every resident with dignity and respect and protect each resident's rights under G.S. 131D-21, including freedom from abuse, neglect and exploitation, privacy, private communication and telephone access. Staff may not abuse, neglect or exploit residents. Under G.S. 131D-2.1, abuse includes the willful or grossly negligent infliction of pain, injury or mental anguish, unreasonable confinement, or the deprivation of needed services by the administrator or staff. Staff may not borrow money from, lend money to, buy from, sell to, or accept gifts, tips, bequests or favors from residents or their families, except as the agency allows in writing. Staff may not handle resident funds or property except under RR-02. Staff may not form personal, romantic, sexual or financial relationships with residents. Staff who see or suspect a violation must report it at once under INC-03. Violations lead to discipline up to and including termination and, where required, a report to the Health Care Personnel Registry and other authorities.

definitions.definition: Willful or grossly negligent infliction of pain, injury or mental anguish, unreasonable confinement, or deprivation of needed services by the administrator or staff (G.S. 131D-2.1).
Failure to provide the care, services or supervision a resident needs, as defined in G.S. 131D-2.1.
Improper use of a resident's funds, property or resources for another person's benefit, as defined in G.S. 131D-2.1.
The limit between a staff member's professional role and personal involvement with a resident, which protects the resident.
Money, goods, services, favors or anything of value given to a staff member by a resident or family member.

procedures: At hire, the Administrator gives each employee this policy. The employee reads it, has questions answered and signs the Staff Conduct Acknowledgment, which is placed in the personnel file.

Staff address residents by their preferred name, knock before entering a room, keep doors and curtains closed during personal care and allow residents to use their own telephone and mail privately, as the residents' rights require.

Staff do not use physical force, threats, humiliation, ridicule, isolation, unreasonable confinement or withholding of food, care or services as punishment or for staff convenience. Use of restraints is governed only by RST-01.

Staff do not ask to borrow money, accept loans, accept gifts of value, tips, or inheritance or named-beneficiary status from residents. A staff member offered a gift politely declines. If a resident insists, the staff member gives it to the Administrator, who documents it and decides how to respond.

Staff do not buy, sell or trade property with residents, do not sign as witness or agent for a resident, and do not hold a resident's debit card, PIN, checks or cash. Any handling of funds follows RR-02.
Staff do not enter personal, romantic, sexual or financial relationships with residents. They do not share personal social media with residents or post anything about residents (RR-04).
Staff do not drink alcohol, use illegal drugs or misuse prescription drugs while on duty (ALC-01) and do not take or use any resident's medications.
Staff do not discuss residents outside the home or in public areas of the home, and do not photograph or record residents without written consent, in keeping with RR-04.

Staff who see, hear of or suspect abuse, neglect, exploitation or misappropriation report it immediately to the Administrator, or to the manager if the Administrator is involved or unavailable, and follow the reporting steps in INC-03. Staff are never punished for a good-faith report.

When an allegation names a staff member, the Administrator separates the staff member from the resident without delay, protects the resident, starts an investigation and reports as required in INC-03.
The Administrator investigates and documents every conduct complaint, interviews those involved, reviews the facts and decides on the discipline within [INVESTIGATION TIMEFRAME].

Discipline is progressive (verbal warning, written warning, suspension, termination), except that abuse, neglect, exploitation, theft or misappropriation, being impaired on duty, or breach of boundaries may result in immediate termination.

Where a finding involves abuse, neglect, exploitation or misappropriation, the Administrator makes the report to the Health Care Personnel Registry and any other agency required under INC-03 and documents the date and confirmation.
The Administrator reviews this policy with all staff at least annually during in-service training and documents attendance.

responsibilities.duty: Enforces the standards, investigates complaints, imposes discipline, makes required registry and agency reports and protects staff who report in good faith.
Models and enforces the standards on assigned shifts and escalates any allegation to the Administrator at once.
Follow this policy, report violations immediately and keep professional boundaries with residents and families.

documentation: Signed Staff Conduct Acknowledgment
In-service attendance sheets
Gift refusal/disclosure log
Conduct investigation reports and discipline records
Registry and agency report confirmations (see INC-03)

policies.title: Administrator Certification and Manager Designation
policies.applies_to: ACH and FCH
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] is always led by a properly certified or approved administrator and that a qualified manager is designated to run the home when the administrator is absent.
policies.policy: The administrator of the home is [ADMINISTRATOR NAME]. For an adult care home (7 or more beds), the administrator holds a current adult care home administrator certification issued under G.S. 90-288.14. The requirements are age 21 or older, completion of the 120-hour Administrator-in-Training (AIT) program (at least 20 hours of coursework and 100 hours of on-the-job training), passing the administrator exam ($50 fee), and a criminal background check. Renewal costs $30, and 30 continuing education hours are required every 2 years after the first renewal. For a family care home (2–6 beds), the administrator holds approval under 10A NCAC 13G .1501, which requires a high school diploma or GED, the State-approved 120-hour AIT program, passing the Administrator Exam, age 21 or older, and a criminal background check. There is no renewal fee for family care home administrator approval. Administrator exams move online starting 9/25/2026. The Administrator confirms the current procedure on the ACLS forms page before scheduling. [AGENCY NAME] designates in writing a manager who is 21 or older with a high school diploma or GED and who completes 12 continuing education hours per year, to take responsibility for day-to-day operation in the administrator's absence. When the administrator position is vacant or the administrator leaves, the licensee notifies ACLS and appoints a qualified replacement as set out in GOV-02.

definitions.definition: The certified (ACH) or approved (FCH) person responsible for the overall operation of the home.
The State-approved 120-hour program for new administrators, made up of at least 20 hours of coursework and 100 hours of on-the-job training.
A person designated in writing to be responsible for day-to-day operation in the administrator's absence (10A NCAC 13F .0102 and Rule .0402), who is 21 or older with a high school diploma or GED.
Required annual or biennial training to maintain certification, which for ACH administrators is 30 hours every 2 years after first renewal, and for managers is 12 hours a year.
Authorization by the State to serve as administrator of an adult care home (certification) or family care home (approval).

procedures: Before the home is licensed, the licensee identifies the administrator and verifies that the person meets the age, education, training, exam and background check requirements for the home type (ACH: G.S. 90-288.14; FCH: 10A NCAC 13G .1501).

If the person has not completed the process, the licensee enrolls them in the State-approved 120-hour AIT program, confirms the schedule for the 20 hours of coursework and 100 on-the-job hours and tracks progress on a written checklist.

The applicant submits the criminal background check request early. The SBI check costs $14, or $38 with the FBI check, and results can take about 2 weeks for the State and up to 12 weeks for the FBI. The licensee records the request date and expected receipt date.

The Administrator confirms the current exam registration steps, fees ($50 for ACH) and online format (available starting 9/25/2026) by checking the ACLS forms page or calling ACLS at 919-855-3765, and records the confirmation.
After the person passes the exam and receives the certificate or approval letter, the Administrator places a copy in the personnel file and posts it as required in GOV-02.

The Administrator enters the certification expiration and CE due dates in the training matrix. For ACH administrators, 30 CE hours are tracked per 2-year cycle after the first renewal, and the $30 renewal fee is paid before the due date. For FCH administrators, the approval is kept current and CE records are kept as ACLS requires.

The licensee names a manager in writing, using the Manager Designation form, who is 21 or older with a high school diploma or GED. The Administrator checks proof of age and education and keeps copies in the personnel file.
The Administrator posts a list showing the manager on duty and how to reach the Administrator and the manager by phone at all times. The list is updated each time the schedule changes.
The manager completes 12 CE hours each year. The Administrator keeps the certificates and checks the total each quarter.
The Administrator briefs the manager before each planned absence on current residents' conditions, incidents, pending reports, appointments and how to reach the Administrator and emergency contacts.
If the Administrator will be absent for an extended period, the licensee confirms with ACLS what is required and documents the arrangements.

If the administrator leaves or the certification lapses, the licensee notifies ACLS as required in GOV-02, places a qualified person in charge in the interim, begins the process to appoint a certified or approved replacement and documents each step and date.
[AGENCY NAME] reviews administrator and manager qualifications at each annual policy review (GOV-03) and before the license renewal (GOV-02).

responsibilities.duty: Appoints a qualified administrator and manager, pays fees, makes sure the administrator keeps certification current and notifies ACLS of changes.
Maintains certification or approval and CE, designates and oversees the manager, keeps records and is reachable at all times.
Runs day-to-day operations in the administrator's absence, completes 12 CE hours a year and reports issues to the Administrator.

documentation: Administrator certification or approval letter
AIT completion record, exam result and background check result
CE certificates and renewal receipts
Written manager designation
Manager proof of age and education and CE certificates
Posted coverage and contact list
Written confirmations from ACLS about exam procedures

policies.title: Resident Records and Retention
policies.applies_to: ACH and FCH
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] keeps complete, accurate, secure and accessible records for every resident, and retains them for the required time.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] keeps a record for each resident that includes the resident's assessment, care plan, medication administration records (MARs), physician orders, the signed contract, and the resident register. The assessment is completed within 30 days of admission, annually, and after a significant change of condition (10A NCAC 13F .0801). The care plan, based on that assessment and including the resident's preferences, is kept where staff can access it (10A NCAC 13F .0802). Records are available to staff who need them to care for the resident and to ACLS and county DSS staff who are authorized to review them. Resident records are confidential and are protected as required by RR-04 and the privacy safeguards of 45 CFR 164.530. The retention period for resident records was not verified when this manual was prepared. The Administrator confirms the required period with ACLS and records it in the retention schedule. Until it is confirmed, no resident record is destroyed.

definitions.definition: All documents about a resident's admission, assessments, care plan, orders, medication administration, incidents, services and discharge.
Medication Administration Record, the document on which each medication given, refused or missed is recorded.
A record of all residents admitted, with admission and discharge dates and contact information.
A written list of each type of record, how long it is kept and how it is destroyed.
A major change in a resident's physical, cognitive or psychosocial condition that requires a new assessment.

procedures: At admission, the Administrator or designee opens a record for the resident and adds the signed contract (CON-01), resident information, physician orders, emergency contacts, advance directive information (RR-03) and any legal representative documents.

The designated assessor completes the resident assessment using the DHSR instrument or an equivalent within 30 days of admission, then annually and after a significant change of condition, and files it in the record (ADM-02).
The care plan is developed from the assessment, includes the resident's care preferences, is signed and dated, and a current copy is kept where staff who care for the resident can access it (ADM-03).
Staff record each medication given, refused or omitted on the MAR at the time of administration and file each month's completed MAR in the record (MED-01, MED-02).
The Administrator files every physician order in the record on the day it is received and makes sure the MAR and care plan match the current order.
Incident reports, change-of-condition notes, physician and family notifications and hospital transfer documents are filed in the record (INC-01, HLT-03).
The Administrator keeps the resident register up to date, adding each admission, discharge, transfer and death with the date on the day it happens.
Each record is kept in a locked cabinet or access-controlled electronic system. Only staff with a need to know may use it, and the record is not left unattended or visible to visitors.
Records are kept available on site for review by ACLS and county DSS staff during a survey or monitoring visit. The Administrator keeps a log of outside persons who view records.
Information is released to others only with the resident's or legal representative's written authorization or as the law permits (RR-04). The Administrator documents every release.

The Administrator audits a sample of resident records each month for completeness, including assessment dates, care plan currency, physician orders and MARs, and writes up any gap and its fix (GOV-04).
Staff correct an error in a record by drawing a single line through it, writing the correct entry with the date and their initials, and never obliterating the original.

The Administrator contacts ACLS at 919-855-3765 to confirm the required retention period for resident records and for the resident register, writes the answer, date and source in the retention schedule and reviews it at each annual policy review (GOV-03).

Until the retention period is confirmed and recorded, no resident record is destroyed. After it is confirmed, records are destroyed only after the period ends, by shredding or secure electronic deletion, and the destruction is logged with the date and the name of the person who did it.
When a resident is discharged or dies, the Administrator closes the record within [CLOSE-OUT TIMEFRAME], checks it is complete, and moves it to secure storage under the retention schedule.

responsibilities.duty: Ensures records are complete, secure and accessible, confirms the retention period with ACLS, audits records and controls release and destruction.
Maintains records in the Administrator's absence and makes them available to authorized surveyors.
Complete assessments, care plans, MARs and notes accurately and on time, and protect resident confidentiality.

documentation: Resident record (assessment, care plan, MARs, physician orders, contract)
Resident register
Record audit forms
Record access and release log
Retention schedule with ACLS confirmation
Record destruction log

policies.title: Required Reports to the State
policies.applies_to: Adult Care Home (10A NCAC 13F) and Family Care Home (10A NCAC 13G). Where a rule is cited only for the Adult Care Home, the Family Care Home follows the corresponding Subchapter 13G requirement and, at minimum, the procedures in this policy.
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] submits every required report, renewal, notice and filing to the NC DHHS Division of Health Service Regulation, Adult Care Licensure Section (ACLS), the county Department of Social Services (DSS), local emergency management, residents and responsible persons, and the NC DHHS Office of the Controller, accurately and by the due date, with proof of each submission kept on file.
policies.policy:
[AGENCY NAME] reports to the State completely, accurately and on time. The Administrator, [ADMINISTRATOR NAME], is responsible for the reporting calendar and for each submission. This policy sets the dates and recipients for the recurring and event-driven reports below. It points to the owning policy for incident, abuse and registry reporting, and it does not replace those policies.

1. Annual license renewal. The facility files its license renewal annually on a calendar-year basis with the nonrefundable renewal fee (10A NCAC 13F .0208 for Adult Care Homes; 10A NCAC 13G .0208 for Family Care Homes). The renewal discloses ownership and states bed capacity and census data. An Adult Care Home with an Alzheimer's special care unit also reports that unit's bed capacity. The facility understands that uncorrected violations can lead to an extension of the plan of correction, a provisional license, or denial of renewal.

2. Evacuation reports. If residents are evacuated, the facility reports to local emergency management, the county DSS and ACLS within 4 hours of the decision to evacuate. It reports to the same three agencies again within 4 hours of the residents' return (10A NCAC 13F .0309). The facility follows this practice in the Family Care Home as well.

3. Change of licensee. The current licensee gives written notice to ACLS, the county DSS and each resident or responsible person at least 30 days before a change of licensee (10A NCAC 13F .0207). The prospective licensee files the change application, fire and sanitation reports dated within 12 months, and the fee.

4. Closing of the home. The facility gives written notice to ACLS, the county DSS and each resident or responsible person at least 30 days before closing (10A NCAC 13F .0211). The notice states the closing date and the plans for moving residents.

5. Notice of revocation. When the facility receives a notice of revocation of its license, the Administrator tells each resident and responsible person in writing of the notice and its basis within 5 calendar days (10A NCAC 13F .0212).

6. Adult Care Cost Report. A facility that receives Special Assistance or is an exempt facility prepares and submits the Adult Care Cost Report to the NC DHHS Office of the Controller. The next report is due September 30, 2027. The Administrator checks the Office of the Controller's current instructions each year. Those instructions state that an agreed-upon-procedures (AUP) report is no longer required for facilities with 7 or more beds for fiscal periods beginning on or after July 1, 2026.

7. Incident, abuse, neglect, exploitation, missing resident, death and registry reports are made within the timeframes and to the agencies stated in INC-01, INC-03, MIS-01, HLT-08 and STF-02. The Administrator logs each of those reports in the State Reporting Log required by this policy so that all reports can be reviewed in one place.

Any report that is late, incomplete or found to be inaccurate is corrected immediately and reviewed through GOV-04.

definitions.definition: The NC DHHS Division of Health Service Regulation, Adult Care Licensure Section, which licenses adult care homes and family care homes. Phone 919-855-3765; email DHSR.AdultCare.Questions@dhhs.nc.gov.
The county Department of Social Services in the county where the facility is located, including its Adult Home Specialist, who monitors the facility with ACLS.
The person designated in the resident's record who is authorized to act for or receive notices on behalf of the resident, such as a legal representative or family member.
The Administrator's dated list of recurring report deadlines, including license renewal, fire and sanitation report dates, drills, and the Adult Care Cost Report.
The facility record showing every report or notice made to a state or county agency, with date, time, recipient, method, the staff person who made it, and proof of receipt or transmission.
The movement of residents out of the facility because of fire, disaster or other emergency, as described in FIR-01 and FIR-02.

procedures: By January 15 of each year, the Administrator updates the reporting calendar. It lists the license renewal filing, the fire and sanitation report dates, quarterly fire drill dates for each shift, the Special Assistance and Medicaid cost reporting dates, and any plan of correction due dates.

Before the renewal filing, the Administrator compiles ownership information, current licensed bed capacity, Alzheimer's special care unit capacity if applicable (Adult Care Home), and current census data from the resident roster. A second person (the Manager or owner) reviews the figures for accuracy.

The Administrator files the annual license renewal on a calendar-year basis, with the nonrefundable fee, before the due date set by ACLS. The renewal fee is $360 plus $17.50 per bed for an Adult Care Home, as invoiced by ACLS, and $315 for a Family Care Home. The Administrator checks the invoice against these amounts and contacts ACLS at 919-855-3765 if the amount differs.

The Administrator keeps a copy of the filed renewal, the fee payment record and the ACLS confirmation in the licensing file. If the renewal is not confirmed within 14 days of filing, the Administrator contacts ACLS to confirm receipt.

If a survey leaves violations uncorrected, the Administrator reviews the plan of correction, due dates and status with the owner. The Administrator documents each correction with date and evidence, and requests an extension from ACLS in writing before the due date if a correction cannot be completed.

When an evacuation is decided, the Administrator or the person in charge assigns one staff member to make the notifications. That person records the time of the decision. Within 4 hours of that time, the staff member notifies local emergency management, the county DSS and ACLS (919-855-3765), and records the time, the person spoken to and the method in the State Reporting Log.

When residents return, the same staff member records the time of return and, within 4 hours of it, repeats notice to local emergency management, the county DSS and ACLS. The Administrator records the evacuation and return reports in the State Reporting Log and attaches them to the evacuation after-action review under FIR-02.

If the owner plans a change of licensee, the owner informs the Administrator at once. At least 30 days before the effective date, the current licensee sends written notice to ACLS, the county DSS and each resident or responsible person. The notice states the planned effective date and the name of the prospective licensee. A copy of the notice is placed in the licensing file, and each resident or responsible person signs or the facility documents mailing or delivery.

Before the change of licensee date, the Administrator helps the prospective licensee assemble the change application, the fire and sanitation reports dated within 12 months, and the fee. This is documented in the licensing file. The Administrator also confirms with the owner that residents' records and funds are handled under REC-01 and RR-02 for the transition.

If the owner decides to close the home, the Administrator prepares a written notice stating the closing date and plans for moving residents. The notice goes to ACLS, the county DSS and each resident or responsible person at least 30 days before closing. The Administrator documents delivery to each person and keeps the copies. Resident moves follow ADM-05 and the closure steps in GOV-02.

If the facility receives a notice of revocation of its license, the Administrator reads it on the day it arrives and informs the owner. Within 5 calendar days of receipt, the Administrator gives each resident and responsible person written notice of the revocation notice and its basis, by hand delivery or mail, and documents the date and method for each person.

The Administrator reviews any report required by INC-01, INC-03, MIS-01, HLT-08 or STF-02 within one business day of the event to confirm that it was made on time to the right agency. The Administrator enters it in the State Reporting Log. If a deadline was missed, the Administrator makes the report immediately and records the reason for the delay.

Each year, the Administrator checks the NC DHHS Office of the Controller's Adult Care Facilities page and any notices received to confirm whether the facility must file the Adult Care Cost Report. If so, the Administrator or the facility's accountant prepares it from the facility's financial records and submits it by September 30, 2027, and then by the due date in each later instruction. The Administrator keeps the submission confirmation and workpapers.

Each month, the Administrator reviews the reporting calendar and the State Reporting Log for upcoming and overdue items. The Administrator signs and dates the review. Overdue items are reported to the owner within one business day.
Each quarter, the Administrator reports on state filings, deadlines met and missed, and open plan-of-correction items to the governing body or owner as part of GOV-04.
The Administrator keeps all submissions, confirmations, notices and correspondence for the retention period in REC-01, and makes them available to ACLS and the county DSS on request.

official.notes:
NC has no single plan-of-operation form. The reviewing documents are two near-identical ACLS desk-review checklists (DHSR/AC 4649 for ACH, DHSR/AC 4648 for FCH, both Rev. 04-2014). The ACLS Licensure Consultant works through each section, checks it off on a blank line, and signs 'Desk review completed. Required policies and procedures have been verified.' The forms do not number their items. Section order is the form's order. The item_ids (1-15, with sub-letters a, b, c... for the checkbox lines) are only ordinal labels I added, and the rule cites are the forms' own.

Process: for the ACH, the Construction Section notifies ACLS of the new project, and ACLS then contacts the applicant for 'the application, policies and procedures.' For the FCH, once ACLS receives the packet from the county adult home specialist, it 'sends a letter to the applicant requesting submission of certain records, policies and procedures for review.' The county adult home specialist also meets the applicant to review the operational plan. The DSS specialist's emphasis areas are doc 2 above. The policies are not submitted with the license application or fee.

Submission: organize the manual in the checklist's section order so each checkbox can be located. Include actual documents where the form asks for them: the fire evacuation plan, the disaster plan, a one-month sample menu with portion sizes (RD-signed therapeutic menus if used), an activity calendar with start and end times, and the resident contract. Medications are covered by the separate optional DHSR Form AC 4640 'Guidelines for the Development of Medication Administration Policies and Procedures', which I did not fetch, so I did not list its content. ACLS also posts an optional Template Infection Prevention & Control Policies and Procedures for ACHs and FCHs (DOCX) on its Forms page, which I did not fetch. The AC 4649/4648 forms are dated 2014 even though the rules were readopted effective 9/1/2024, so the rule cites may have been renumbered. Confirm the current rule numbers with ACLS (919-855-3765) before citing them.
